items.text:
Why can't we get rid of antibiotic resistance?
November 21, 2026
"The threat is immense," said Jean Pierre Nyemazi, acting director of the World Health Organization's department of antimicrobial resistance, during a virtual press conference recently. "An estimated cumulative number of 39 million deaths directly attributable to AMR [antimicrobial resistance] would occur in the next 25 years."
It was, however, the stated goal of World Health Organization, or WHO, member statesto reduce the mortality rate caused by AMR by 10% until 2030, Nyemazi added. "When we see the trend, the investments, the action, we don't think we are on the right track."
Without antibiotics, today's modern medicine would not exist
A world without effective antibiotics would be like traveling back to the days in which even the smallest infection was life-threatening, said Can Imirzalioglu, director of the Institute of Medical Microbiology at Justus Liebig University Giessen. "If antibiotics were no longer effective, modern medicine as we know it today would no longer be possible at all."
Imirzalioglu is not only an expert on antibiotic resistance but also on "One Health," a concept adopted in 2004 by experts in human medicine, veterinary medicine and nature conservation. It recognizes that the health of humans, animals and the environment is closely interconnected.
After all, antibiotics and antimicrobial-resistant germs are not just a problem in hospitals. They can also be found in animal shelters, in animal products, in waste water, in fertilizers and in plants. "One Health tries to keep an eye on all of this," Imirzalioglu said.
For hospitals and doctors' offices this means that antibiotics must be used as selectively and purposefully as possible. To this end, research is focused primarily on developing better and faster diagnostic methods.
In Germany, antibiotics were frequently prescribed against respiratory or urinary tract infections, Imirzalioglu said. But antibiotics are only effective against bacteria. If a virus causes the infection, they are ineffective.
Nonetheless, every antibiotics dose has consequences: it damages our gut microbiome. This consists of billions of micro-organisms, primarily bacteria, which are essential for digestion, metabolism and the immune system. "If we damage the [bacteria], resistant pathogens can spread and take their place," Imirzalioglu said.
Another problem was that such a spreading of resistant pathogens in the gut often went unnoticed and without causing symptoms, he added.
So people became "carriers of resistant pathogens, which they, in turn, release back into their environment."
In this way, resistant pathogens make their way out of hospitals via toilets and sinks into wastewater and, from there, into the Baltic Sea, where they are ingested by wild birds. This pathway was traced in a study by Katharina Schaufler, a veterinarian and microbiologist at the Helmholtz Institute for One Health (HIOH).
Why factory farming exacerbates the problem
Antibiotics have not only been used in humans on a large scale over a long time, excessive use in veterinary medicine has also led to resistance to nearly all available antibiotics, Schaufler said.
In 2006, an EU-wide ban on the use of antibiotics as growth promoters in animal feedcame into effect. Since then, antibiotics may only be applied as part of veterinary treatment.
The problem is that due to factory farming the use of antibiotics for medical purposes is a permanent necessity. The mere fact that animals live together in confined spaces causes infections to spread rapidly.
Lack of space as well as boredom lead the animals to injure each other and this happens in an environment where, in Schaufler's words, "there's already a high level of bacterial pressure."
Through fertilizers, antibiotic-resistant pathogens enter the environment. "It has been proven that, for example, resistant bacteria can still be found on lettuce heads," the veterinarian said. Resistant bacteria were also found time and again on meat.
National solutions are also falling short. In many countries, antibiotics are still a standard additive in animal feed, Schaufler said. And in such countries, antibiotics could be obtained in drugstores without prescriptions, Imirzalioglu added. Both say that all of this makes the global fight against antibiotic resistance more difficult.
Combating antibiotic resistance means preventing infections
Political will is of the essence when it comes to combating antibiotic resistance. Imirzalioglu works at Guardian, a project funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space.
The aim of the project is to prevent outbreaks of diseases caused by resistant bacteria by monitoring and analyzing wastewater in the German state of Hesse.
At EU level, Imirzalioglu is also an advisor at the Antimicrobial Resistance One Health Network. He sums up his experience with policymakers: "The experts and working groups have great ideas, and then these are often scaled back or stifled during the initial stages."
Perhaps the lack of political will so far is one of the reasons why the WHO's Nyemazi is issuing an appeal to every individual: Preventing antibiotic resistance means preventing infections, through hygiene, regular vaccinations and doctor's appointments as well as taking medications in accordance with prescriptions.
This article was originally published in German.

items.text:
'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?
- Published
It is rare when a key handball decision is given for the widespread response to be "that is correct".
Often the discussion centres on the desire for a seemingly more lenient interpretation taking into account perceived intent.
And that is again a talking point after the crucial penalty given against Chelsea in Saturday's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds which ended up putting the visitors ahead for the first time.
Interestingly, despite the perception, handball penalties are much rarer in the Premier League compared with the other top five leagues in Europe.
Last season, there were 22 penalties for handball in the English top flight's 380 games - easily the lowest tally.
Spain's La Liga (36) and Italy's Serie A (38) produced the most.
This season in the Premier League there have been three in 106 matches - less than in 2025-26.
So why was the penalty given against Chelsea's Morgan Rogers?
Why the penalty was given
The feeling among Premier League clubs is that handball is in a good place now, where the arm must either be fully extended away from the body, raised, or be a deliberate act to be punishable.
And it is the last of these that applied to the penalty given against Rogers, which to some might seem a bit harsh, considering the Premier League's more relaxed interpretation of handball.
There are, however, a few key reasons why referee Michael Oliver pointed to the spot, why the video assistant referee (VAR) did not intervene, and why it will be judged as a correct decision.
Two of the factors which a referee looks for when judging a potential handball apply here.
First, how far the ball travelled.
As Jayden Bogle's shot was from distance, a defender is considered to have more time to adjust their body and react - and thus avoid a potential handball.
Most important in this case is the movement of the arm.
When Bogle shoots, Rogers' arm is not raised - but it comes up to the flight of the ball.
Crucially, had Rogers kept his arm in its original position - lower and level with his midriff - there would not have been a handball offence.
What does this mean? Put simply, if the ball would have hit the body if it had not come off the arm, it is considered to have no impact.
But this case was different. Rogers raised his arm and that is what led to the ball being deflected away. This is considered a deliberate act, and this trumps all other considerations.
Was there any case not to give it?
Perhaps there was a question about whether the ball hit Rogers too high on his arm, and thus should not be a handball offence.
It was close, but it looked like it was in what the laws call the 'red zone', the part of the arm which is punishable for handball.
But this really would be the only reason the VAR, Michael Salisbury, would have any cause to consider an on-field review.
We saw a similar case last season, in terms of how this kind of handball offence is judged - coincidentally involving a penalty awarded to Leeds.
As Anton Stach's powerful strike arrowed towards goal, Everton defender James Tarkowski leaned to his left in an attempt to block the shot - and did so with his arm, which was tucked tightly to the side of his body.
Everton manager David Moyes described the decision as "wrong", but it was absolutely correct in law.
That Tarkowski's arm was close to his side was irrelevant because of the deliberate act of leaning into the path of the ball.
Likewise, Rogers raised his arm to stop the ball and a penalty was a justifiable call.
Decision underlines dissatisfaction with handball law
Despite the Premier League having a more lenient interpretation of the handball law already, it is clear that many observers would like it to go further.
For example, BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer echoed many when he said there should be more intent for a handball.
"I didn't agree with the penalty when Michael Oliver gave it," he said.
"I know once the on-field decision is made there is a high bar to review it, but I don't think officials are allowed to use common sense.
"Morgan Rogers is not deliberately trying to stop the ball. He just doesn't want it hitting him in the face.
"Although the penalty came at an important point in the match, Chelsea were deservedly beaten by a much stronger, far more physical and better-organised Leeds team."
Rogers may argue he raised his arm to protect his face.
This is one of the possible mitigating factors, but usually only applies when a player raises their hands to their face - not using the arm as a barrier.
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso said that, while he did not "want to make a big thing about it", the penalty should not have been awarded.
"For me it was quite a harsh decision," he told Sky Sports. "I would not have given a penalty. I don't want to make a big thing about it but for me it's not a penalty."

items.text:
Mexican special forces arrest drug kingpin 'Chapo Isidro'
November 21, 2026
A gun battle between Mexican soldiers and alleged gang members in the city of Guasave, in the state of Sinaloa, ended with special forces detaining senior members of the Beltran Leyva drug trafficking network, Mexican officials said on Saturday.
The gang is aligned with one of the factions of the powerful Sinaloa cartel.
Authorities said the overnight raid resulted in capture of the suspected drug kingpin Fausto Isidro Meza F., better known as "Chapo Isidro," who is believed to be the leader of Beltran Leyva.
FBI offering millions for 'Chapo Isidro'
The 44-year-old Mexican national is one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives. The US law enforcement agency claims his group is responsible for smuggling "large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States," and has offered a $5 million (€4.56 million) reward for information leading to his arrest.
He is also wanted in Mexico on charges including organized crime.
On Saturday, Mexican authorities said the raid was conducted due to "intelligence coordination" between Mexico's military and US agencies.
The three detainees were transported to Mexico City "to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities," the military said.
It was not immediately clear if "Chapo Isidro" will be extradited to the US.
Roads blocked in Sinaloa
The troops used "stealth and surprise" to reach the area, establishing a perimeter around the drug dealer's location and then moving in from multiple directions, according Mexico's US embassy.
Unverified videos from Guasave, however, showed military helicopters firing at ground targets and sports fans scrambling for safety during a baseball game. Some of the violence in the western Mexican city seems to have taken place after Chapo Isidro was arrested, with drug cartels attempting to retaliate against the authorities and civilians for the move.
Mexico's defense ministry confirmed cartel members set up roadblocks in the area, but added that security forces were assisting local authorities in restoring order.
The Guasave raid is only the latest in a string of high-profile moves against senior leaders of Mexico's illegal drug trade. Less than two weeks ago, Mexican navy announced the arrest of Rafael A., suspected of leading a cartel cell active in the states of Jalisco and Michoacan.
President Claudia Sheinbaum is facing pressure from Donald Trump, who has threatened to take military action against cartels on Mexican territory.
Editor's note: DW follows the German press code, which stresses the importance of protecting the privacy of suspects, victims and those who are associated with a criminal case, and urges the media to refrain from publishing their full identities in most cases.

items.text:
Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
Before worrying about the temperature of the turkey, travelers could face a different type of uncertainty next week. This time, it's the weather — and it's affecting both U.S. coasts.
"I know there's a lot of travel for many of you as you head into the Thanksgiving holiday, but I'm going to ask you all to consider not traveling unless it is absolutely essential," said San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie on X Friday. He said the city is preparing this weekend for extreme high tides and rain that could hit the area Monday afternoon through Wednesday.
Over the past week, cities in California saw mudslides, waterspouts and flooding while Florida also saw coastal flooding and inundated streets. A new set of storms are expected to hit both sides of the country early next week, just as travelers head into the holiday week.
It's already been a wet fall in large swaths of the country, thanks in part to a Super El Niño, a natural climate pattern that shifts weather around the world. Devastating flooding in the Southwest U.S. left multiple people dead and hundreds stranded, and California and the Pacific Northwest have seen high sea level and multiple strong atmospheric rivers.
Atmospheric rivers are here to stay
"Take this weekend: get yourself ready," Lurie, the San Francisco mayor, said after a call with the National Weather Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
Rain and snow, in higher elevations, is possible over parts of the northwest and northern California on Saturday, according to the NWS.
The West Coast is forecasted to see an atmospheric river, a narrow band of water vapor pushed by the wind, on Monday. Another is expected for the Pacific Northwest later in the week, according to the Center for Western Weather and Water Extremes. Atmospheric rivers hang over an area and dump precipitation. They can cause months worth of rain in just a few days.
The center expects two to four inches of precipitation over northern California and southern Oregon through Wednesday.
Coastal flood advisories are also in effect through Monday morning in the Bay Area, the NWS said. This comes on top of historic high tides, known as King tides.
Travel troubles could persist after Thanksgiving
A storm that started in Florida Friday will move north to the Mid-Atlantic and into the Northeast by Sunday evening, according to the NWS.
Some of the heaviest rain could be seen on the coast of the Carolinas through Sunday morning. Then, heavy rain is expected to move up the coast, said Dan Hoffman, a meteorologist at the National Weather Service in Baltimore, Md.
Hoffman said during a busy travel week, even with the weather not expected to bring flooding or strong winds, it "doesn't usually take too much to cause things to start to have delays."
As for New England, Andrew Loconto, a meteorologist at the NWS in Norton, Mass., said the storm this weekend is not forecasted to be as big as another storm hitting the region after Thanksgiving. "That could be more impacts for people coming back home," Loconto said, pointing to another highly anticipated day across the U.S. — Black Friday.

items.text:
Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
- Published
A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic Kaliningrad territory has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say.
The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday, and drifted into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack.
"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said, adding: "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."
Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones were used, according to preliminary information, and that there is "no threat" to their supplies.
The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and American governments.
The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011, and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.
On Saturday morning, Finnish defence forces detected the drone attack on the cargo vessel west of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland, which prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" over the area.
Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".
A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship, and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way."
The Finnish Border Guard also said the crew had not been forced to abandon the ship, no environmental damage had been detected, and there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.
Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.
Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said that the Finnish Border Guard are responsible for the investigation into the attack, and are cooperating with other relevant authorities.
Nato has also been informed, the defence ministry said.
The Baltic Sea has become a flashpoint in the Russia-Ukraine war, triggered when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has recently ramped up its long-range attacks against Russia beyond the front lines.
Earlier this month, a Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland.

items.text:
FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach: Reports
The reported hacking is the latest in a string of breaches and outages affecting the US government.
The FBI’s national criminal database has suffered a suspected breach, according to multiple US media reports.
President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly downplayed breaches affecting departments within his administration, appeared to confirm the FBI hacking during a television interview on Saturday.
“Well, we just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that,” Trump told Fox News.
On Friday, CNN and NBC reported that the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share information on criminal warrants and background checks, was compromised, citing two people who had been briefed on the matter.
The reported hacking, which would be the second to hit the bureau this year, is the latest in a string of US government breaches and outages that have alarmed officials over the past week.
In a separate incident, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture.
The FBI and USDA did not immediately return Al Jazeera’s request for comment.
In the interview on Saturday, Trump suggested the hack of the FBI’s crucial database could be viewed with “a positive spin”.
“Maybe we’ll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise. You had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. You had all these other hoaxes,” he said in an apparent reference to his discontent with the FBI’s investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 US election.
In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber group that claimed it had stolen sensitive information on the bureau’s 38,000 employees.
Additionally, in March, the agency said it had been investigating “suspicious activities” on some of its internal systems, The Associated Press news agency reported.
FBI Director Kash Patel, who has not publicly commented on the most recent hacking, was not present for a Wednesday hearing at the US Capitol to examine threats against the US. Patel’s deputy, Christopher Raia, attended in his place, joining US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

items.title: Scottish Premiership roundup: Celtic sweep St Mirren aside to strengthen grip at top
items.summary:
The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership.
The centre-forward Camilo Duran was also o
items.text:
The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1. The champions brushed off the loss of midfield pair Mika Baur and Benjamin Nygren to injury to consolidate their place at the top of the Premiership.
The centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes. Callum McGregor grabbed his first league goal of the season before Killian Phillips scored a consolation from the spot.
With Baur facing up to 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Nygren nursing a heel problem, Martin O’Neill would have been delighted with how his midfield functioned.
Oxlade-Chamberlain made his fifth start of the season and McCowan his second. The pair had never started a game together before. O’Neill also introduced the former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joël van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old showed some good touches.
Celtic started with a new-look front three of Duran flanked by Jota and Yang Hyun-jun. Duran was a constant threat and had two goals disallowed for offside in the opening quarter.
Yang was instrumental in the 33rd-minute opener, racing past Declan John and drilling a low pass which ultimately fell for Oxlade-Chamberlain to stroke into the bottom corner.
The South Korean soon passed up a brilliant chance, opting to look for Duran when played clean through by the goalkeeper Sam Johnstone. The pass was under-hit and Alex Gogic cleared.
Duran was on the end of a far better ball in the 40th minute, cushioning home a volley after a superb whipped cross by Kieran Tierney. Duran soon set up Jota, who was denied by Jacob Chapman, before finding Tierney, who provided another assist as McCowan drilled a first-time finish.
Celtic went four ahead in the 63rd minute when the ball broke for McGregor on the edge of the box. The captain quickly shifted the ball on to his right foot and swept it into the bottom corner.
Johnstone blew his chance of a clean sheet when he crashed into Calvin Ramsay as he came off his line to punch the ball. Phillips converted the resulting 70th-minute penalty and St Mirren kept pushing with Johnstone saving well from Ismeal Kabia and Samuel Ramos coming close.
The on-loan Chelsea forward Shim Mheuka was handed the chance to impress for Celtic but the game fizzled out for the home side.
Mario Frick enjoyed a dream start to life as Aberdeen manager by edging a six-goal thriller with a 4-2 win at Kilmarnock. Kevin Nisbet’s double along with Brad Lyons and Findlay Marshall strikes secured three priceless points to leave the Rugby Park side rooted to the bottom
The visitors climbed to eighth spot after a remarkable afternoon where the Pittodrie side hit a much-needed scoring streak. Aberdeen opted to dispense with the services of Stephen Robinson after a run of one win from seven which saw them sink to second bottom and Frick was appointed as his replacement last Sunday.
Dundee United recorded their biggest ever win at Easter Road with an impressive 4-0 thrashing of Hibernian. Zac Sapsford’s first-half double laid the foundations before Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall found the net after the break.
The visitors were well worth the three points as they cemented their place in the top six and picked up their first win in Leith since 2021. It was a humbling afternoon for Hibs, who thought they had turned a corner under their new head coach, Marink Reedijk, after back-to-back victories before the international break.
Falkirk clung on to clock up six top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1966 with a 2-1 home victory against St Johnstone. John McGlynn’s team scored early in each half to remain third.
Jacob Murrell’s eighth goal of a superb debut season sent Falkirk on their way inside six minutes. Finley Barbrook’s second goal in as many games on 48 minutes doubled the advantage. Josh Campbell nodded in a late reply to serve up a scare but the hosts held firm.

items.text:
Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off violence
MEXICO CITY — Gunfire rang out, trucks burned and Mexican forces clashed with cartel gunmen in the state of Sinaloa overnight as Mexican authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro."
Meza Flores was one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives and a top cartel leader from the Beltrán Leyva criminal organization wanted for trafficking drugs to the United States and illegally carrying firearms.
Mexico's government said in a report early Saturday that intelligence from the Trump administration helped authorities capture him, but provided few details about how authorities in Mexico and the United States coordinated to detain Meza Flores.
He was also a key ally to "Los Mayos," a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which was designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the Trump administration last year. His capture represents a blow to the cartel as it fights with another faction for control of the northern Mexican state.
Authorities in the United States and Mexico celebrated the arrest as a security win. U.S. President Donald Trump has pressured Mexico's government to go after criminal groups.
But experts warn that it could set off another wave of violence in a region already caught up in a power struggle between warring cartel factions.
Mexican forces' move against cartel fuels violence
Mexican authorities said they used "stealth and surprise" to capture Meza Flores, establishing a security perimeter around the building where he was located. After coming under attack with guns and explosives from suspected cartel operatives, armed forces personnel entered a home and detained him. He was later taken by aircraft to Mexico City to appear before prosecutors.
Video shared by authorities shows heavily armed men in camouflage escorting a man through a dimly lit house and putting him in the back of a truck. No casualties have been reported so far as a result of the operation.
The capture of Meza Flores and his No. 2 in the city of Guasave, Sinaloa, set off a wave of violence overnight with calm setting in Saturday morning.
Videos show screaming civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, burning cars and businesses, and circling helicopters shooting at people below. Such shows of force by cartels are common following the capture or killing of leaders.
As a result, the Mexican army and National Guard special forces were unable to extract Meza Flores from Guasave until 4 a.m. on Saturday, said a federal official who spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorized to discuss the case.
"Getting him (Meza Flores) out was extraordinary," the official said, describing an intense response by members of the criminal group who maintained at least "10 roadblocks" with burning vehicles on Guasave's streets.
Terror in Sinaloa
Guasave resident and firefighter Paola Sánchez said that thousands of people were terrorized late Friday as they took shelter from intense gunfire in grocery stores and other locations.
"Last night, many businesses were burned ... along with cars and trucks," Sánchez told The Associated Press.
She said that the city's firefighters had to take shelter at their station and wait until Saturday morning for orders from their superiors to dispatch the first crews to check whether any businesses or vehicles were still burning.
"Everything looks calm today," Sánchez said.
Mexican Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch wrote on X on Saturday morning that armed forces would remain deployed in Sinaloa state to protect civilians.
Capture prompts celebration and warnings
Meza Flores' detention marks another high-profile capture of a cartel leader as Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum faces pressure from Trump to crack down on cartels. Sheinbaum has gone after illegal groups more aggressively than her predecessors, and homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office.
The U.S. and Mexican governments celebrated the capture on Saturday, with the DEA commending Mexican authorities.
"The capture of El Chapo Isidro delivers a significant blow to a ruthless criminal organization that has used extreme violence to traffic deadly drugs, including fentanyl, a designated weapon of mass destruction, into American communities," the DEA said in a statement. "This operation underscores the critical importance of intelligence sharing in targeting dangerous cartel leaders."
García Harfuch called the detention "an important step in pacifying Sinaloa."
Sheinbaum's government has targeted a number of cartel kingpins, including Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, known as " El Mencho," who was killed by the military in February.
Mexican security analyst David Saucedo said that the capture of Meza Flores marked another case of the governments of Mexico and the U.S. increasingly falling back on a longstanding security strategy, which critics warn could fuel more violence in the long run.
The so-called kingpin strategy relies on zeroing in on capos like Meza Flores as a way to combat cartels. But experts say that it often triggers violent power disputes among groups, like the one underway in Sinaloa.
"What is evident is this is a product of pressure from the United States," Saucedo said. "What they do is capture high-profile kingpins — the leaders — but they don't dismantle the entire organization. They arrested the No. 1 and No. 2, but the entire network of hit men, street-level drug dealers, businesses and political and police connections remains intact."

items.title: European football: Noslin’s double helps Lazio extend Serie A lead; Nmecha sends Dortmund top
items.summary:
Lazio continued to underline their Serie A title credentials with a comfortable 3-0 home win against Lecce as Gennaro Gattuso’s side remained unbeaten this season and extended their lead at the top of the standings.
Tijjani Noslin scored in each half and Davide Frattesi wrapped up the win in style w
items.text:
Lazio continued to underline their Serie A title credentials with a comfortable 3-0 home win against Lecce as Gennaro Gattuso’s side remained unbeaten this season and extended their lead at the top of the standings.
Tijjani Noslin scored in each half and Davide Frattesi wrapped up the win in style with a 90th-minute strike as Lazio earned their 10th victory in 12 games to move to 32 points, four ahead of Inter who travel to Atlanta on Sunday. Como are fourth on 26 points after a 2-0 win against Cagliari thanks to goals from Jacobo Ramón and Lucas Da Cunha.
The majority of Lazio fans continue to boycott home matches in protest against the club owner Claudio Lotito, yet the unrest has done little to unsettle Gattuso’s players. “I look at it the other way around,” Frattesi told Dazn when asked about being top of the league. “We’re on 32 points, with eight still to go [for 40 points which usually guarantees survival].”
In Germany, Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha fired his side to the top of the Bundesliga table as they won 1-0 at bottom side Borussia Mönchengladbach. After Bayern Munich were held to a 1-1 draw at home by Cologne on Friday, Dortmund capitalised to take a two-point lead at the summit.
The home side played far better than their position would suggest, withstanding waves of pressure from the visitors, but Gladbach finally cracked in the 80th minute when Nmecha picked up the ball on the edge of a packed penalty area and let fly. Unsighted by the thicket of bodies in front of him, the goalkeeper Daniel Batz misjudged the trajectory of the ball, and it flew over his right shoulder and into the net.
Gladbach created a number of chances, but Gregor Kobel came to the rescue with several fine saves for Dortmund, and once the goal went in, there was no way back for the hosts. Dortmund have 24 points after 10 games, two ahead of Bayern and third-placed Freiburg, who beat Elversberg 1-0.
Fourth-placed RB Leipzig had five different players on the scoresheet in a 5-1 drubbing of Union Berlin that lifted them to 21 points. Bayer Leverkusen thumped four goals without reply past Paderborn to remain fifth. Eintracht Frankfurt remained in the running for the European places thanks to a 1-0 win against Hoffenheim, with Jonathan Burkardt’s first-half goal securing the victory.
Meanwhile, Fifpro said on Saturday it was “deeply concerned” by public comments from Bayern’s leadership about Jamal Musiala’s contract, accusing the German champions of putting pressure on the midfielder while he recovers from health problems. The global players’ union was responding to recent remarks by senior Bayern officials, including honorary president Uli Hoeness, chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, about Musiala’s future at the club.
Hoeness earlier this month questioned whether the 23-year-old Germany international could return to his previous level after being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. Dreesen later backed those remarks, saying Bayern would evaluate Musiala’s progress and discuss his future with his representatives. Rummenigge subsequently defended the comments, saying the club’s consideration of Musiala’s health and contract situation was both responsible and normal.
“Bayern’s honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract in quick succession,” Fifpro said in a statement. “In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.”
Musiala signed a contract extension with Bayern until 2030 in February last year. He has endured a difficult run of injuries and health setbacks in recent months. He broke his leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025, missed half of last season and collapsed twice within a few days in August before being diagnosed with a neurological disorder. In September, he suffered a hamstring injury.
“Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury,” Fifpro added. “Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.”
Dreesen rejected suggestions that Bayern were trying to pressure Musiala. “We all hope that Jamal will be the Jamal we know again,” Dreesen said on Saturday. “He needs time to come back. We’ve said that several times now. He has to be given that time. And then we’ll see how things look at the beginning of next year.”
Dreesen added that there was no need to keep talking about Musiala’s contract. After September’s injury, Musiala returned as a substitute in Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday in which Harry Kane sustained an injury that may mean months of rehabilitation.
On Saturday, Kane said he was looking to come back improved for “the business end of the season”. Kane tore a ligament in his left ankle and Bayern said the Ballon d’Or winner had undergone “successful surgery overnight” having earlier said that Kane would be out for “the next few months”.
Kane posted a photo on Instagram of himself smiling broadly, while sitting on a hospital bed after the surgery, with his leg encased in a medical boot. “The highs and lows of life!” the 33-year-old wrote. “Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.”
- This story will be updated

items.title: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid
items.summary:
The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s top 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that trigg
items.text:
The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s top 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that triggered widespread panic in the city of Guasave.
The alleged leader of a major drug-trafficking cartel, the Meza Flores Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO), he had managed to evade arrest for more than a decade, even though there was a reward of up to $5m (£3.8m) on his head.
His FBI “most wanted” poster states his organisation “is allegedly responsible for the possession, distribution, and importation of large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States, and has predominately controlled drug production, transportation and distribution in several locations throughout Mexico”.
Mexico’s defence ministry also alleged he is the leader of the Beltrán Leyva criminal organisation, which is allied to the Mayos, one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel.
Meza Flores’s alleged second-in-command, Germán N, whose alias is “Serafín”, and José N, an alleged financial operator for the Beltrán Leyva group, were also arrested.
The operation to capture the men was carried out by “elite military forces” with help from US intelligence, according to Mexico’s defence ministry.
After arriving in the “target area … using stealth and surprise”, the ministry said the arresting force came under attack “with gunfire and explosives” but managed to enter a house and make the arrests.
The men were then evacuated to Mexico City on a Mexican air force plane to be handed over to prosecutors.
Videos and photos show civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game at Kuroda Park stadium in Guasave, as well as burnt-out cars.
A barrage of rapid fire from what appeared to be Mexican security force helicopters fired at the ground, according to CNN, and players from the Venados de Mazatlán and Algodoneros de Guasave teams abandoned the field mid-game.
Meza Flores was originally indicted in 2012, and in 2013 the US Treasury placed sanctions on him under the Kingpin Act, freezing his assets.
In 2017, the US Department of State’s Narcotics Rewards Program began offering up to $5m as a reward for information leading directly to his arrest or conviction.
He has been charged with multiple counts of drug-trafficking violations, and use and possession of a firearm in the US, and was wanted in Mexico for organised crime and offences against public health.

items.text:
Fifpro criticises Bayern Munich for Musiala comments
- Published
Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better".
Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".
Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness said earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had".
The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned, external the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested, external the deal may need to be renegotiated.
"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," said a Fifpro statement.
"In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better."
- Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness 
  - Published9 November
- Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala? 
  - Published19 August
Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September.
He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist.
"Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.
"Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.
"Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise."
Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months".

items.title: Liverpool vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
items.summary:
Liverpool vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
One of sport’s biggest rivalries takes centre stage as Liverpool host a Man United side in the EPL relegation zone.
Who: Liverpool vs Manchester United
What: English Premier League
When: Sunday, November 22 , at 4:30pm (16:3
items.text:
Liverpool vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
One of sport’s biggest rivalries takes centre stage as Liverpool host a Man United side in the EPL relegation zone.
Who: Liverpool vs Manchester United
What: English Premier League
When: Sunday, November 22 , at 4:30pm (16:30 GMT)
Where: Anfield in Liverpool, United Kingdom
How to follow: Al Jazeera will have full text commentary coverage of the game with build-up from 13:30 GMT
The latest rebuild of Manchester United begins at Liverpool on Sunday with Mauricio Pochettino in the hot seat – a position that some see as the impossible job.
The match at Anfield comes four days after the arrival of the Argentinian, who only oversaw his final game as United States coach on Wednesday.
The 54-year-old is tasked with ending a 13-year wait for a 21st Premier League title – only Liverpool have won the competition as many times as the Red Devils.
United sacked Michael Carrick last week with the team third from bottom in the league and suffering their worst league start for 40 years.
Pochettino is the ninth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired with the club’s last league title in 2014 and he is the fourth in the last three years.
United’s recent pain is made worse by Liverpool’s revival in the last decade, with the Reds sitting fourth in the table and hoping to mount a challenge this season to move clear as the team with the most English top-flight titles.
What were the key takeaways from Pochettino’s Man United media conference?
Given the swift turnaround from his previous role to his new one, Pochettino’s unveiling as United manager was combined with the pre-game media briefing ahead of the Anfield trip.
Understandably, most of the questions centred on how United’s form can be reversed in the short and long-term.
“It is about building our own way here,” Pochettino said when asked what he can do differently to the other managers who have taken on the role since Ferguson’s farewell. “The past is not going to help, to think about yesterday.”
“We feel the support and we are going to work really hard to help the players to perform. That is the priority.
“It is normal when you don’t win games that the confidence starts to go down,” he said. “I think the players need to feel from us that we believe and trust in them.
“With the schedule we have ahead we have to settle on our principles. The players are intelligent, they have quality. Sometimes it is unlocking some things that didn’t appear for different reasons.”
A key figure in any rebuilding effort will be captain Bruno Fernandes, whose future has been the subject of speculation as he has yet to agree a new deal.
Pochettino revealed he had already held extensive talks with the Portugal midfielder and indicated he remained central to his plans.
“Bruno is our captain and a very important player but other players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top,” he said.
“We spoke, I spent three hours chatting with all the players individually. It was very nice contact.”
Questions about the squad’s fitness levels have swirled around Old Trafford, but Pochettino refused to criticise what he had inherited.
“It is about proposing that idea to be brave and take it to the field,” he said.
“We cannot talk about data without context. It is easy to manipulate data but we need to be honest, sometimes they don’t show something that you can see on the field.
“We are here not to denounce things. We are here to build something with our players.”
What have Liverpool said ahead of Manchester United’s visit?
Liverpool had lost consecutive games before their 3-1 win against bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace in their last match.
The run summed up the mixed start to life at Anfield for Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer – the former Bournemouth manager admits an epic encounter awaits.
“You don’t find bigger games than this, honestly. I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be part of these games,” Iraola said.
“We have to acknowledge the importance of the game, and also a lot of ingredients, such as their new manager.
“It is important for us in lots of different ways because we want to improve our form at home and the first chance we have to do that is on Sunday.”
Iraola also admitted he fears Pochettino, whose Premier League experience was gained at Tottenham and Chelsea, will have an advantage because he does not know the Argentinian’s preferred tactics with his new club.
“We’ve faced each other. Obviously he has a lot of Premier League games that we can look at and we can look at games in the US, but they still have this small advantage,” Iraola said.
“We don’t have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we don’t actually know.
“The staff have been working with them, so they are going to arrive well prepared. We don’t have the references that we have against other teams.”
Iraola will have to adapt on the fly and the Spaniard plans to switch up his game plan if he is caught out by Pochettino’s tactics.
“Especially the beginning of the game will be important as we have to adapt to certain things and manage the situation as quick as possible,” he said.
“Every time there is a new manager you want to impress. It happens everywhere. But we have been focusing more on us, how we can improve.”
What happened the last time Liverpool played Man United?
United were 3-2 winners when the sides met in the Premier League at Old Trafford last season.
Liverpool fought back from two goals down in May, only for Kobbie Mainoo to net the late winner from the edge of the box.
What happened in the corresponding fixture last season?
United were 2-1 winners at Anfield in October last year, with Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire scoring either side of Cody Gakpo’s strike.
When did Liverpool last beat Manchester United?
Liverpool last beat United with a 3-0 win at Old Trafford in the Premier League in September 2024.
Luis Diaz scored twice and Mohamed Salah netted

items.summary:
Chelsea beaten 4-1 by Leeds to suffer third loss in four in Premier League
Leeds come from a goal down at Stamford Bridge to shock Chelsea and climb above their hosts to sixth in Premier League.
Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds as the Blues were beaten for the third time in
items.text:
Chelsea beaten 4-1 by Leeds to suffer third loss in four in Premier League
Leeds come from a goal down at Stamford Bridge to shock Chelsea and climb above their hosts to sixth in Premier League.
Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches.
Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart on Saturday by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.
Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London.
Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment.
Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon.
Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period.
Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman.
Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute.
Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home.
Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front.
Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil.
Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool.
While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager.
Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss.
Bournemouth and Tottenham on the rise in Premier League
Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.
Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game, and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries’ winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games.
Tottenham are also marching up the table after a difficult start to the campaign.
Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of a 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi’s men.
Thomas Frank’s arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles’ fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table.
Dwight McNeil’s late own goal gave the Sky Blues a vital victory in their quest for survival back in the top flight after four goals were shared in a thrilling first half.
Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone.
Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday, with the Red Devils second from the bottom of the table.

A Russian attack on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s hometown of Kryvyi Rih has killed two people and wounded 60
items.text:
Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown
Attack on Kryvyi Rih comes as Russian missiles land in NATO member Poland and US-led peace efforts face uncertainty.
A Russian attack on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s hometown of Kryvyi Rih has killed two people and wounded 60 others, according to local officials.
The strikes hit the central Ukrainian city on Friday night, killing a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while six children were among the injured.
About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and businesses were damaged, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of Kryvyi Rih’s city administration.
Vilkul said on Saturday that Russian forces launched further missiles after emergency workers arrived, hitting rescuers, medical personnel and utility crews.
Footage released by Ukraine’s emergency services appeared to show additional strikes during the rescue operation.
Russian attacks elsewhere in Ukraine killed two people in the southern Zaporizhia region, according to its governor.
Russian authorities also reported six deaths, including a child, from a Ukrainian attack on a residential area in Russian-controlled Luhansk, an eastern Ukrainian region.
The violence followed a separate incident on Friday in which two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in southeastern Poland, a member of NATO, the military alliance linking the United States, Canada and European countries.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident on Friday as a deliberate provocation, questioning its timing alongside military exercises involving European countries preparing for a possible post-war security mission in Ukraine.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte condemned the airspace violation on Saturday and pledged that the alliance would defend Polish territory.
The incidents have unfolded as US President Donald Trump seeks progress in negotiations with Moscow and Kyiv.
Trump said on Friday, following talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China, that the Russian leader wanted to end the war diplomatically.
Zelenskyy, however, told reporters in Kyiv on Saturday that he remained less convinced than Washington that Putin was prepared to compromise.
Moscow continues to demand Ukrainian withdrawal from the entire eastern Donbas region, which Kyiv refuses to surrender.
Zelenskyy also reaffirmed Ukraine’s ambition to join NATO, while Washington has discussed offering Kyiv security guarantees resembling the alliance’s collective-defence commitments.
Such guarantees remain under discussion as negotiations continue over how to end the war and protect Ukraine from future attacks.

Lincoln City vs Wrexham; Sky Bet Championship
Lincoln City vs Wrexham. Sky Bet Championship.
LNER Stadium.
Watch match highlights
Lincoln 0-1 Wrexham: George Thomason nets winner for Red Dragons
Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Lincoln City and Wrexham at the ProAmpac Stadium on Saturday; George Thomason scores the only goal as Red Dragons claim a narrow late victory.
Saturday 21 November 2026 17:45, UK
George Thomason grabbed a late winner as Wrexham secured a welcome 1-0 victory away at Lincoln.
It was a game lacking real quality in the final third at Sincil Bank.
But Thomason kept his cool when the moment arose to fire Wrexham to victory with his 82nd-minute strike.
It was a first away league victory for Phil Parkinson's charges since the start of September when they beat Millwall 2-0.
The Red Dragons have now gone three games without defeat and will be hoping to use their recent upturn in form as a catalyst towards their play-off push.
For Lincoln, it was the latest bump in the road as the reality of being minnows in the Championship is really beginning to hit home.
Any hopes the international break would bring about a change in fortunes were dashed with a fourth loss on the spin, whilst it is their seventh defeat in nine.
Their only victory in that time was the 4-1 hammering of relegation rivals Burnley, which led to Nicky Hayen's sacking.
The first real chance of the contest fell to the visitors as Callum Doyle nodded wide of the mark from Thomason's delivery into the box.
Down the other end, Rob Street saw his own header well kept out by stopper Anthony Patterson.
Defender Demi Elerewe produced a great double block when he prevented Ollie Rathbone from breaking the deadlock.
Patterson was then called into action once more to deny Adam Reach's effort on the half hour mark after good link up play between Reach and Dan Oyegoke.
Street came close to changing the complexion of the respective half-time team talks when he agonisingly fired wide on the stroke of the break.
The second half was a poorer showing than the first with meaningful chances at a premium after the restart.
George Wickens got down low to keep out Rathbone's tame strike from outside the box in a routine bit of keeping.
Patterson barely had to move to stop Andrei Coubis' effort down the middle of his goal.
Dom Jefferies' free-kick did not threaten the visitors, whilst Oyegoke was kept out by another routine Patterson stop heading into the final quarter of an hour.
But the door was eventually unlocked when Thomason snatched the winner with eight minutes to go.
The 25-year-old pounced on a poor back pass and easily slotted home a left-footed effort beyond the on-rushing Wickens for his second goal of the campaign and most importantly to secure the points for the Welsh outfit.
Lincoln chucked on reinforcements to try and salvage something from the game.
Bailey Cadamarteri was denied Wrexham's second, with Patterson keeping out Jefferies right at the end.

items.text:
Bolton Wanderers vs Portsmouth; Sky Bet Championship
Bolton Wanderers vs Portsmouth. Sky Bet Championship.
Toughsheet Community Stadium.
Bolton 1-1 Portsmouth: Sam Dalby earns point for Trotters
Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bolton Wanderers and Portsmouth at the Toughsheet Community Stadium on Saturday; Josh Murphy nets early for Pompey before Sam Dalby hits back for Trotters as spoils are shared.
Saturday 21 November 2026 17:45, UK
Bolton nemesis Josh Murphy helped Portsmouth secure a 1-1 Championship draw at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.
Murphy's first goal of the season put Pompey in front but Sam Dalby ensured Wanderers avoided a fourth successive home defeat with his seventh goal of the season and third in four games.
Despite this frenetic opening 12 minutes neither side could celebrate a first game back after the international break with three points.
Murphy ensured the worst case of deja vu for Wanderers, now unbeaten in 15 second-tier games against Pompey but still adjusting to life after leaving League One last term.
He scored the two first-half goals that saw Oxford stun the Trotters in the 2024 League One play-off final at Wembley.
This time it took him seven minutes to register his opening goal of the campaign and first since March 2025, heading in a deep right-wing cross from Northern Ireland international Terry Devlin.
But Steven Schumacher's side crucially levelled five minutes later. Max Conway, atoning for giving possession away for the game's first goal, crossed from the left and Dalby side footed home inside the six-yard box.
Goalkeeper Nicolas Schmid, however, should have done better as he allowed the striker's shot to go through his legs in front of his own supporters.
Top scorer Dalby should then have put Bolton in front in first half stoppage time.
Excellent work by Sam Iling-Junior fashioned the chance but Dalby could not convert the winger's cross on the slide from four yards.
Portsmouth, beaten only once now in seven outings, started the second half positively with Murphy seeing a shot deflected for a corner.
Bolton though were more than a match for their visitors as they looked to improve this season's dismal home form.
Schmid saved from midfielder Xavier Simons' shot as both sides rang the changes in an attempt to make the breakthrough.
Portsmouth's hopes of a second goal though were repeatedly dashed by a succession of offsides while Wanderers
Teenager Max Lott headed wide shortly after entering the fray while defender Chris Forino tested Schmid in the final stages of normal time with a close-range header.
Forino was the focal point for Bolton's late raids but again Schmid comfortably dealt with his latest attempt via a Lewis Brunt cross.

items.text:
Stoke City vs Birmingham City; Sky Bet Championship
Stoke City vs Birmingham City. Sky Bet Championship.
Bet365 Stadium.
Watch match highlights
Stoke 1-0 Birmingham: George Hirst scores as 10-man Potters claim win
Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Stoke City and Birmingham City at the bet365 Stadium on Saturday; George Hirst nets the winner as 10-man Potters then hold on to topple the Blues.
Saturday 21 November 2026 17:24, UK
George Hirst scored the only goal of the game as 10-man Stoke moved into the automatic promotion places with a 1-0 victory over Birmingham.
Hirst broke the deadlock in the early stages of the second half before Luca Bombino was shown a second yellow card for the hosts in the 63rd minute.
The two teams were level on points towards the top of the Sky Bet Championship at the start of the day, with Birmingham top and Stoke third.
Both had won their last three games, and it was the hosts who prevailed as Hirst scored for the first time since early September.
Despite seeing 10 of the 20-man matchday squad that beat Portsmouth last time out go away on international duty, it was the hosts who came out of the traps quickest.
Jack McGlynn took up a deeper role in Stoke's midfield in the absence of Northern Ireland international Ethan Galbraith, one of four changes to the Stoke side from the win at Fratton Park, and the American fizzed a long-range shot past the upright inside the first two minutes.
Bombino also returned to the Potters' starting XI and was picked out by McGlynn's inviting back-post cross, heading his effort against Ethan Laird and out for a corner.
The American forced the returning James Beadle into his first save shortly afterwards, working space for a shot on his lesser-favoured right foot.
As Blues struggled to contain Mark Robins' side in the early stages, McGlynn played in Ben Johnson, who forced Beadle to push his low effort around a post.
Beadle and top scorer August Priske were both back in Blues' starting line-up after missing the last two games with injury, while Seung-ho Paik replaced Jhon Solis, who was absent from the squad.
It took Birmingham half-an-hour to register a shot as Phil Neumann met Alex Cochrane's corner, only to see his header saved by Viktor Johansson.
Bae Junho was making his first start in over a month and should have done better with Bombino's bobbling cross but headed his effort comfortably wide of Beadle's left-hand post.
Stoke started the second half in similar fashion to the first and were ahead within three minutes of the restart.
Bombino played in Djibril Soumare who whipped in a cross from the left which Hirst calmly turned beyond Beadle, scoring just his second goal since moving from Ipswich in the summer.
Stoke almost doubled their lead just past the hour with a free-flowing counter-attack. Hirst played in Johnson down the right and he was denied by the huge frame of Beadle.
Seconds later, the hosts were down to 10. Already on a booking, Bombino's strong challenge on Patrick Roberts earned him a second yellow card.
Blues went about trying to make their man advantage count through Demarai Gray, whose inswinging cross was diverted wide at the back post by Laird.
Birmingham threw on a plethora of attacking options in the closing stages as the clash became attack against defence, as Marvin Ducksch glanced Roberts' cross narrowly wide.
Jay Stansfield's curling effort was beaten away by Johansson as Stoke stood firm to remain joint-top of the table.

Swansea 2-2 West Brom: Managerless Swans hit back twice for a point
Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea City and West Bromwich Albion at the Swansea.com Stadium on Saturday; Managerless Swans hit back twice to earn a point as Isaac Price misses a penalty for the Baggies.
Saturday 21 November 2026 17:27, UK
Ashley Williams began life as Swansea's interim head coach with a draw against the club who showed him the door as a 16-year-old 25 years ago.
West Brom led twice through goals from Isaac Price and Rabby Nzingoula, but Swansea levelled each time thanks to Moussa Yeo and Eli Just.
All the goals came in an eventful first half, with the crucial moment being a penalty save by Swans goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux to deny Price.
Williams, who took over in midweek after Vitor Matos quit to join Strasbourg, had to watch his team cling on as Albion missed a hatful of late chances.
Baggies substitute Aune Heggebo thought he had won it but his stoppage-time effort was ruled out for offside.
Swansea's season was upended at the start of the week with Matos' shock decision to leave for France.
Less than a year after taking charge and just four months after signing an extended contract, the Portuguese coach quit for Ligue 1.
That forced the Swans to draft in an old-boys quartet of Williams, Joe Allen, Leon Britton and Kristian O'Leary, with former Wales captain Williams leading the interim coaches.
Writing in the Swansea match programme, chief executive Tom Gorringe said: "There is no denying that we are disappointed with the events of the week."
The club are reported to have agreed a £5million compensation package with Strasbourg.
The disruption seemed to spread confusion through Swansea's defence and after West Brom had twice gone close, they went ahead through Price in the seventh minute.
Kareem Tunde was allowed space on the right and fired a low cross to where an unmarked Price finished at the far post.
There was an immediate response from Swansea and Adam Idah forced Max O'Leary in to a fine save, before Yeo levelled after 16 minutes.
A slick passing sequence on the left sliced Albion's defence apart, allowing Josh Tyman to find Yeo, who headed home from close range.
After Swansea's Scotland international Stephen Welsh had been treated for a clash of heads with Brayann Pereira, the centre-back twice came to his team's rescue with last-ditch tackles.
But there was nothing he could do to prevent Nzingoula putting Albion 2-1 ahead in the 38th minute, when a corner was flicked on by Jayson Molumby.
Tymon then gave away a penalty for holding Molumby, but Price tried a flashy 'Panenka' which Vigouroux was able to gather, even though he had initially dived the wrong way.
Swansea made the most of their lucky break by making it 2-2 in the fourth minute of first-half stoppage time.
A long ball was deftly laid back by Jisung Eom into the path of Just, whose low drive from 20 yards arrowed into the far corner.
The second half mostly belonged to the Baggies with a Molumby shot deflecting wide off Melker Widell, before Harry Whitwell and Felix Myhre went close.
The nearest Swansea came to a goal was when Just's chip bounced off the top of the crossbar.
The result leaves West Brom fifth in the table, with Swansea back in eighth, two points behind.

items.text:
West Ham United vs Preston North End; Sky Bet Championship
West Ham United vs Preston North End. Sky Bet Championship.
London Stadium.
Watch match highlights
West Ham 1-1 Preston: Konstantinos Mavropanos earns a point for Hammers
Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between West Ham United and Preston North End at the London Stadium on Saturday; Konstantinos Mavropanos heads home in second half to earn a point for the Hammers but Scott Parker stays winless.
Saturday 21 November 2026 17:11, UK
Scott Parker's stuttering start as West Ham manager continued in his first match at the London Stadium as bottom club Preston battled their way to a 1-1 draw.
Parker is yet to taste victory in three games since he returned to the club he once graced as a player.
After Konstantinos Mavropanos headed home on the hour to cancel out Liam Lindsay's early goal for the visitors, it seemed that West Ham's attacking power would force a victory to keep pace in the Championship promotion race.
Instead, in spite of 27 efforts on goal, they could not break Preston's resistance and are now winless in their past five games.
If the second half was one-sided, the first period was anything but. The only surprise was that it contained just a single goal.
Joel Piroe ought to have done better than shoot into the legs of Preston keeper Lee Nicholls after being sent clear by Arne Engels before Lindsay fired the visitors ahead in the 18th minute.
An inswinging Alfie Devine corner was met by Piroe whose flicked header looped backwards and inadvertently struck his own crossbar before dropping down for Lindsay to lash it over the line from two yards out.
West Ham responded with an Edson Alvarez shot into the side netting following a corner of their own.
The Preston goal had an extraordinary escape in the 27th minute when Joel Veltman set up Jarrod Bowen whose shot cannoned back off the left-hand post and into the path of Veltman who instantly struck the other upright.
If that was unfortunate, the home side had a lucky escape minutes later when Thierry Small opened up space for himself in the West Ham area but then lifted his shot wastefully over the bar.
A frantic game became even wilder as half-time approached.
Divine Mukasa dragged a shot wide for West Ham before their 20-year-old keeper Finlay Herrick justified Parker's decision to hand him a Championship debut.
Herrick threw himself to his left to parry away a Callum Lang shot, before springing up to save Devine's follow-up.
The beginning of the second half was just as hectic with Edvin Austbo jinking inside and curling his shot against the same part of the crossbar that featured in Preston's goal.
Leaving just one man up, the visitors dropped deeper and deeper, challenging West Ham to force their way through for the equaliser.
Bowen neatly set up Alvarez only for the Mexican to drag a weak shot wide. Eventually the Preston defence gave way with Mavropanos rising highest to head home an Engels cross.
Having drawn themselves level, West Ham continued to drive forward only for their play to become more desperate at times, mirroring the anxiety among their fans.
Their bombardment of the Preston goal almost brought its reward deep into injury-time only for Nicholls to brilliantly tip over a Tomas Soucek header.

items.title: Noah Okafor piles on pain for Alonso as rampant Leeds demolish dismal Chelsea
items.summary: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since returning to the top of the table with a
items.text:
Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since returning to the top of the table with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.
It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty early in a one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that it was easy to conclude they would have won even without a helping hand from the officials.
Farke’s side were tactically superior, better coached and far more determined than their flimsy opposition. Chelsea, who briefly led through Emmanuel Emegha, were comprehensively outplayed and could not complain about being jeered off at the end of their fifth defeat in 11 games.
These are worrying times for Alonso. Chelsea lost Moisés Caicedo to an early injury and have not developed a clear way of playing since appointing the Spaniard – unless, of course, the identity is supposed to revolve around a defence completely addicted to calamity.
It has been difficult to work out exactly what Alonso wants Chelsea to be. Are they a passing side or a counterattacking one? Do they mix it up and do both? One quality absent from their defeat against Sunderland was physicality. Chelsea were chewed up and spat out at the Stadium of Light and the recent lack of flow has not been helped by the ongoing absence of João Pedro in attack.
Something different was required and initially there was a more balanced feel to Chelsea with Emegha, making his first start since joining from Strasbourg, leading the line. They made a fast start but their equilibrium was disturbed by Caicedo making way for Jordan Henderson after injuring his back in a collision with James Justin. The shift in momentum was instant and it was against the run of play when Leeds fell behind to a sharp finish from Emegha in the 25th minute.
The visitors had threatened in the air, Calvert-Lewin sending one header against the bar and another straight at Emiliano Martínez, but they were undone by poor defending at the other end. There was nothing clever from Chelsea, simply a hopeful punt down the left, and Leeds would have been fine if Justin had timed his header properly. Instead the defender’s clearance hit Rogers and ran nicely for the Chelsea forward to release Emegha, whose vicious shot flew past James Trafford at the goalkeeper’s near post.
The goal should have settled Chelsea’s nerves. Yet Leeds stayed calm and levelled within three minutes. Chelsea have no leaders at the back, especially with Maxence Lacroix absent with a hamstring injury. Wesley Fofana is too easily ruffled in the air and was partly at fault for the equaliser. He sent a routine header back into dangerous territory and Leeds were in business when that mistake was followed by Josh Acheampong mistiming his jump, leaving Calvert-Lewin to advance through the middle and give Okafor the chance to slip a low shot past Martínez.
Chelsea’s response was feeble. There were times when Leeds simply ran through them. Tarik Muharemovic charged in from the left, away from a lazy Cole Palmer, and saw his cross flicked wide by Calvert-Lewin. Ao Tanaka went close, Calvert-Lewin missed another header and Muharemovic grimaced after having a goal disallowed for offside.
Ethan Ampadu was running the game for Leeds in midfield. Chelsea were being outmuscled again. They were losing all the 50-50s and Levi Colwill, low on confidence since returning from a lengthy knee injury, looked like he wanted the ground to swallow him up when he sent a simple pass out for a throw.
Chelsea were booed off at half-time. Colwill was toiling against Calvert-Lewin and Leeds continued to dominate at the start of the second half, raging when Michael Oliver elected not to award a penalty for Martínez’s clumsy challenge on Calvert-Lewin.
The luck did not last long. Back came Leeds, causing havoc with one of Ampadu’s long throws. The ball dropped loose, Jayden Bogle cracked it goalwards and this time Oliver pointed to the spot after deciding that Rogers had blocked the wing-back’s shot with an arm. It was a controversial call given that Rogers had his arm close to his body and the ball hit him close to the shoulder. Yet the decision was upheld and Leeds were ahead when Calvert-Lewin sent Martínez the wrong way from the spot.
Leeds were relentless and did not have to wait long for a third goal. Ampadu delivered another long throw. Chelsea cowered and Sean Longstaff knocked the ball out to Ampadu, who was unchallenged as he crossed for the unmarked Okafor to beat Martínez with ease.
The closing stages were miserable for Chelsea. Palmer was an irrelevance, Estêvão Willian was awful on the right and Leeds turned the screw in added time. Aaronson, a late substitute, sped down the right, turned past Malo Gusto and smuggled a shot through Martínez’s grasp to complete the humiliation.
