A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.
In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was forced to play its World Cup qualifying games abroad.
That changed last week, as Haitian police and troops from El Salvador reconquered the stadium. Nayib Bukele, El Salvador’s authoritarian president, called the development a step towards delivering Haiti from a criminal insurrection that has displaced more than 1.5 million people and killed thousands.
“We now have the upper hand on the ground,” claimed Bukele, who has sent more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti since mid-October.
Outside the Sylvio Cator stadium, named after an acclaimed Haitian athlete who won a silver medal at the 1928 Olympics, there were joyous scenes as citizens celebrated a foreign politician they hope will prove an unlikely saviour.
“There’s a wind of hope blowing through our country and, thanks to God, we will get through this. Long live Bukele!” said a 55-year-old decorator who asked to be named as Bòs Baton.
Stood by Sanon’s battle-scarred fresco, Baton recalled being driven from an area called Poste-Marchand after criminals set his home ablaze during an armed uprising that started in February 2024. “Today, we are happy because there are places we couldn’t go to before that are accessible – and it’s thanks to Bukele’s intervention that we can be here today,” Baton said.
Identical sentiments have been voiced on the streets of El Salvador’s capital, San Salvador, in recent years as a result of Bukele’s controversial anti-gang crusade, which has freed millions from gang rule – albeit at a high price.
Since that crackdown began in early 2022, more than 90,000 Salvadorans have been jailed as part of a mass incarceration campaign that has slashed murder rates but also fuelled fears that El Salvador’s democracy has died.
Bukele’s domestic clampdown has made the millennial strongman a darling for rightwing politicians and voters across Latin America and the Caribbean, who hold his actions up as proof that, with an iron fist and a malleable approach to human rights, rampant criminality can be tamed.
Now, as Bukele seeks to extend his seven-year presidency in an election in February, he is hoping to burnish his gang-busting credentials overseas.
“It’s an operation that projects force, that projects Bukele’s image as the saviour … and positions El Salvador as a key reference in the region for [how] … to deal with gangs and security,” said Tiziano Breda, a Latin America regional expert from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project.
The extent of Bukele’s ambitions in Haiti is unclear. The operation’s trigger was the 18 October abduction of four Salvadoran aviation technicians who worked for a UN-backed security force. On Monday, Bukele’s vice-president, Félix Ulloa, announced Salvadoran troops would withdraw as soon as the four men were rescued, “because this is not an occupying force – we are not there to stay”.
But Ulloa also said his government was responding altruistically “to a cry for help from the Haitian people and government”, suggesting its mission could be extended.
Bukele has also hinted his plans go beyond short-lived ground operations to recover his citizens, or their remains. “We will triumph. God will give us victory,” the politician vowed this week.
Many Haitians hope his combatants will stay and have been thrilled by cinematic social media clips posted by Bukele showing helicopter strikes on a gang compound and the mansion of a gangster nicknamed Taliban.
Banners and billboards around Port-au-Prince celebrate Bukele as a 21st-century liberator and feature slogans such as “The bandits won’t get a wink of sleep!” and “We’re tired! Give us Bukele!”
Standing outside the liberated football ground, bricklayer Venel Saindor recalled how criminals torched his home in Carrefour-Feuilles three years ago. “It’s impossible to enter my neighbourhood because the thieves are still there. They shoot at us,” the 56-year-old explained, lifting his shirt to reveal a bullet scar above his right nipple.
“We need Bukele to help us return to our homes,” added Saindor, as a Salvadoran soldier with a belt-fed heavy machine gun kept watch from the stadium’s terraces.
Monique Clesca, a writer and activist, echoed the bricklayer’s enthusiasm. “Haitians are elated … [and] I feel elated also … It is a moment of hope,” she said on Tuesday, as thousands of demonstrators poured on to the streets to champion Bukele, chanting: “Viv Bukele!” and “Bukele is not playing games!”
As a sea of protesters swept towards the prime minister’s offices, people from all walks of life spoke of how armed groups had destroyed their lives and their collective hope that Bukele may provide a solution.
“I used to drive an old bus. The bandits burned it. They burned my house down too,” said Wilné Persona, a 50-year-old driver, adding: “Bukele is the one we are waiting for … because we can no longer bear the situation.”
A food vendor called Claudy Mayas urged “Papa Bukele” to stand his ground. “Bukele, I bless you, your wife and your children,” said Mayas, 51. “The Haitian people are with you, just as you are with us.”
Clesca attributed the palpable excitement to the widespread perception that Bukele’s “decisive” action had exposed the incompetence, inefficiency and indifference of Haitian and foreign leaders. “Basically, what Bukele has done is show that leadership is about resolving a problem for your population,” she said, praising how the stadium and other areas were

items.title: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
items.summary:
'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled
items.text:
'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled the Nordic nation, whose proximity to Russia and unusually open public records system make it particularly vulnerable to Moscow’s hybrid war tactics.
For many internet users, the time-saving option of clicking “Accept cookies” while visiting some of Sweden’s most popular websites seemed mostly harmless. Even the companies hosting the websites thought so – to them, the ad-tech groups paying for the data-collecting cookies appeared to be legitimate.
But in at least one case, it was all a front.
In an investigation conducted by Swedish newspaper Dagens Nyheter (DN), potentially sensitive user information was shown to be collected – via a digital front in Luxembourg – and then funneled to a Moscow-based company partly financed by Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich.
Abramovich is the former owner of Chelsea FC and a close ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin. When Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, he was among the first oligarchs to be added to international sanctions lists, forcing him to sell the football club – the proceeds from which are still frozen in a British bank account.
Hundreds of websites
In its investigation, DN was able to trace traffic going from 425 Swedish websites directly to an Abramovich-linked company called Between Digital. Many of the websites, such as online directories Eniro and Hitta.se as well as several digital media platforms, are among Sweden’s most popular, and are used by people every day. Hitta.se, for example, says it registers some 400 million visits a year.
Carl Heath, a senior scientist at Sweden’s state-owned research institute RISE, told the newspaper that since Between Digital has its central server in Moscow, everything it gathers can be readily accessed by Russian authorities like the FSB domestic security and intelligence agency.
“Who looks up whom, from where and when is precisely the kind of data that could be of interest to a foreign power,” Heath explained, noting that the data obtained is much more detailed than simply IP addresses.
Home addresses, court records, dating habits
Some of the websites that Between Digital has been keeping tabs on are platforms that have built their whole business models on Sweden’s unusually far-reaching freedom of information principle.
The principle stipulates that all of Sweden’s official records, save those that have been specifically classified, are available to the public. In practice, this means that anyone can anonymously look up anything from a person’s home address and salary to their date of birth or any court ruling in which they were involved.
And a lot of it is now available online.
Ratsit.se, an online search engine and one of the websites targeted by Between Digital, provides much of this type of data, going as far as to list whether someone is married or what kind of car they own.
Jonas Lejon, a cybersecurity expert and founder of the IT security company Triop, said that the combination of the ability to track online behaviour as well as to extract so much personal information from public records is extremely dangerous.
“You can piece together the puzzle about people. You can profile them to the extent that you know exactly who they are,” he said.
“Ultimately, it could be used to pressure people through blackmail and other threats.”
Familjeliv.se, Sweden’s largest online community and parenting portal, has also been subject to Between Digital’s data collection. In just the past 30 days, the website registered nearly 2 million sessions – and considering that the country's population is under 11 million, that traffic is massive.
Many of the users turning to Familjeliv.se do use aliases to protect their identities, since the topics discussed can be sensitive and range from relationships to issues in the workplace.
‘We didn’t know’
So-called persistent cookies, or cookies designed to remain for longer than a specific online session, can trace a person’s internet activity for weeks or even months unless a user clears their browser cache (a folder that remembers websites the person has visited). The DN investigation did not reveal what type of cookies Between Digital is thought to be using, however.
Mikko Hypponen, recognised as one of Finland’s most prominent cybersecurity experts, said this type of data is a goldmine for intelligence agencies – which can now also use AI to help them extract useful information.
“Data is key to everything today. The more you have, the better, and it’s especially valuable for intelligence agencies and espionage purposes,” he said.
Even when cookies might not be able to determine exactly what a person is doing on a website, the visit in itself can be revealing.
“Let’s say you keep visiting a dating site late in the night, every night, or you go to the website of a psychotherapy centre once a week, or you visit the website for a dependency group like Alcoholics Anonymous. We may have no idea exactly what you did on the site, but we can guess,” Hypponen said.
User data has been misused before. As recently as October, Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli tech-ad firm had used advertising technology to install spyware on some of the media group’s devices. And in 2023, the Washington Post revealed that a conservative Catholic group in the United States spent millions of dollars to track the online behaviour of priests they suspected were gay.
Following DN’s investigation into Between Digital, many of the concerned websites have cut ties with the company and launched internal investigations.
“We didn’t know until you contacted us,” Gustav Kinde, the head of Ratsit, told the newspaper, echoing the reactions of many other company executives.

Usman Khawaja and David Warner were taken off television commentary duties on Saturday until the “Sandpap
items.text:
Usman Khawaja and David Warner taken off air over Australia’s Sandpapergate
Ex-Australia cricketers Khawaja and Warner taken off air having been most outspoken over 2018 scandal in South Africa.
Usman Khawaja and David Warner were taken off television commentary duties on Saturday until the “Sandpapergate” storm passes, with both set to miss Australia’s entire Twenty20 series against England.
The retired pair have been the centre of attention since Khawaja claimed in his autobiography more than two weeks ago that the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball in a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.
Only then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft – who used the sandpaper – were found to be responsible by a Cricket Australia probe.
The move by Fox Sports, for whom they both work, came after Cricket Australia threw its “unanimous support” behind embattled Test captain Pat Cummins.
Cummins denied he knew what was going on and has been under huge pressure since Khawaja’s claims, which were first backed by Warner and then Bancroft.
“In light of recent events, both Usman and Davey will be rested from our broadcasts over the next few weeks,” Fox Sports Managing Director Steve Crawley told Australian media.
“While we always support all members of our commentary team and welcome a diversity of views which is a feature of our summer of cricket, we also understand the pressure they are under to respond to each and every new comment.
“We think it is increasingly difficult to focus on the game while the situation continues to unfold and think it is unfair on both commentators to put them in that position.
“We will continue to monitor the situation,” Crawley said.
It was unclear when they would return, but Australia play four Tests against New Zealand in December-January after the five-game T20 series that got under way in Melbourne on Saturday.
Fast bowler Josh Hazlewood is the latest player from the 2018 side to deny any knowledge of the use of sandpaper and added on Saturday that he would have considered his future had Cummins been removed as captain.

COP31: UN Climate summit runs into overtime as deal remains elusive
Published November 20, 2026last updated November 21, 2026
What you need to know
- Diplomats and delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya, Turkey
- A new draft deal omits any mention of how to phase out fossil fuels, in what campaigners call a step 'backwards' and a 'glaring regression'
- Like in previous years, the climate summit has been extended until a consensus is reached
These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21:
Peru blames 'geopolitical divisions' for lack of COP31 progress
The head of Peru's delegation at COP31, Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, warned that the UN climate summit was unlikely to end with a concrete deal on climate financing or cutting fossil fuel use.
Garrido Sanchez lamented that the outcome "would be very limited."
He reiterated how "geopolitical divisions" were stopping any final deal from mentioning reducing reliance on oil, gas and coal.
The Peruvian delegate singled out major oil producers, such as Gulf Arab states and Russia, as showing significant opposition.
He noted that while Latin American neighbor Panama had also signaled objection to including the term fossil fuels in the final text, Peru was "not so radical" and is keen to attract investment to "ensure our energy security" through renewables.
China throws weight behind '35-by-35' pledge
China has backed a plan proposed by COP host Turkey to raise global electricity demand to 35% by 2035 — up from the current 20%.
In a joint statement with Australia, which is leading negotiations between almost 200 nations at the COP31 summit in Turkey, Beijing said it welcomes "growing international ambition and cooperation ... to increase electricity's share of global final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035 on a voluntary basis."
The statement goes on to highlight the benefits the transition can bring for the economy, jobs, energy security, public health and households.
The two partners also "acknowledge the importance of inclusive climate action that ensures no one is left behind," the text continued.
Dozens of countries, including EU states, Japan, South Korea and Canada, have so far signaled support for the voluntary goal, which aims to boost clean energy use.
Yet, environmental groups have warned that the draft text doesn't stipulate the use of solar, wind and other renewable energy sources, which could allow power plants using natural gas and coal to be included.
COP31: What to expect today
Good morning, and welcome back to DW's coverage of the UN's COP31 climate summit in Turkey.
Negotiators from nearly 200 countries worked through the night to finalize a deal, after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels — the leading cause of climate change.
COP31, being held in the Mediterranean city of Antalya, was due to wrap up on Friday, but has run over time amid deep divisions over fossil fuels.
Hopes are fading that negotiators will finalize concrete plans to drastically slash the use of oil, gas and coal and a deeper commitment to renewable energy.
Stay tuned as we bring you the latest from the closing stages of UN climate summit.
COP31 talks go on — we're taking a break
The UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has gone into overtime, with countries still divided over key issues, including fossil fuels and climate financing.
The talks were scheduled to end on Friday evening, but negotiators have yet to reach an agreement. Germany and several other countries are pushing for a clear commitment to phase out fossil fuels, while poorer nations are demanding more concrete financial support to cope with climate change.
Negotiations are expected to continue into the weekend. We are pausing our live coverage for now and will bring you further updates as talks progress.
WATCH — Turkey's beaches are becoming too hot for sea turtles
While Turkey hosts COP31 in Antalya, a growing climate threat is unfolding on its Mediterranean beaches. Rising sand temperatures are causing most newly hatched sea turtles to be born female, raising concerns about the long-term survival of local populations.
Conservationists warn that climate change, combined with pollution, coastal development and fishing-related injuries, is putting increasing pressure on the species.
DW correspondent Julia Hahn follows the people working to protect Turkey's iconic loggerhead turtles and shows how the climate crisis is already affecting wildlife far beyond the COP31 conference halls.
WATCH — COP climate summit under scrutiny over fossil fuel influence
The UN climate summit in Antalya is drawing criticism from activists and campaigners who question whether global climate talks can deliver meaningful change while fossil fuel interests remain influential. Turkey and Australia, both under scrutiny for their energy policies, are leading this year's conference.
Activists, including Greta Thunberg, argue COP summits have become increasingly ineffective, while others defend them as a vital space to pressure governments. Climate policy experts say the talks have helped reduce projected warming, but stress that real progress depends on action taken by countries between summits, not just agreements reached at them.
WATCH — Maldives environment minister: 'We are not going to live in the dark'
For the Maldives, climate change is already affecting everyday life. Heavy rainfall has forced people from their homes, warmer oceans are damaging coral reefs, and changes in fish stocks are putting pressure on the country's fishing industry. Rising sea levels pose another threat to the low-lying island nation. Meanwhile, global greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise, despite more than three decades of international climate negotiations.

items.title: Uhuru Mourns Former South African Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 — Former President Uhuru Kenyatta has sent a condolence message to South Africa following the death of former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka.
In a statement shared through his official office, Kenyatta conveyed his sympathies to the South African government and people
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 — Former President Uhuru Kenyatta has sent a condolence message to South Africa following the death of former Deputy President Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka.
In a statement shared through his official office, Kenyatta conveyed his sympathies to the South African government and people, as well as the family of the late former Deputy President.
Kenyatta remembered Mlambo-Ngcuka as a distinguished leader whose service to South Africa and contribution to advancing gender equality and women’s empowerment had left an enduring legacy.
The former Head of State also prayed for strength, comfort and courage for her family and the people of South Africa as they come to terms with the loss.
Mlambo-Ngcuka’s death was announced by the South African Presidency on Friday, November 20, with Acting President Paul Mashatile conveying condolences to her family on behalf of the government and the people of the country.
She served as South Africa’s Deputy President from 2005 to 2008, becoming the first woman to hold the position.
She later served as United Nations Under-Secretary-General and Executive Director of UN Women between 2013 and 2021, where she championed gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls.
Her death has drawn tributes from across Africa and the international community, with leaders and organisations recognising her contribution to public service, women’s rights and social justice.

The President said parents should no longer be expected to pay teachers, arguin
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21 – President William Ruto has announced plans to absorb teachers employed by school Boards of Management (BOMs) into the Government payroll, in a move aimed at easing the financial burden on parents.
The President said parents should no longer be expected to pay teachers, arguing that the responsibility of employing and remunerating educators rests with the Government.
“I want all teachers employed by Boards of Management placed on Government payroll. Parents should not continue paying for teachers because that is the responsibility of the Government,” he said.
Ruto spoke at Kipsigon in Mount Elgon Constituency, Bungoma County, on the third day of his development tour of the Western region.
He said the directive forms part of his administration’s affirmative action measures aimed at promoting equity and ensuring learners across the country have equal access to quality education, regardless of their backgrounds.
The Head of State noted that the Government had employed 100,000 teachers over the past four years and would recruit an additional 20,000 next month.
He also highlighted investments in education infrastructure, saying the Government had constructed 23,000 classrooms countrywide to ease congestion and improve the learning environment.
On land ownership, the President reaffirmed his commitment to resolving longstanding disputes in Mount Elgon, where residents have faced challenges securing legal ownership of land.
During the visit, he issued 1,845 title deeds to beneficiaries of the Chepyuk Settlement Scheme Phase III, with a further 2,000 title deeds for Phase II in the pipeline.
“We will make sure that no Kenyan continues living like a squatter in their own country,” he said.
Ruto challenged leaders overseeing settlement schemes to resolve internal disputes and facilitate the issuance of ownership documents to deserving beneficiaries.
The President also cautioned young people against being exploited by politicians to engage in criminal activities or advance political interests.
“Don’t agree to be misused by politicians to commit crimes or engage in blogging for them,” he said.
He instead urged the youth to take advantage of Government empowerment programmes to develop their skills and access economic opportunities.
On the forthcoming General Election, Ruto accused opposition leaders of attempting to undermine the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) through what he termed unnecessary demands.
He argued that the demands reflected a lack of confidence in their electoral prospects, insisting that the electoral agency and other institutions were staffed by competent Kenyans who should be allowed to discharge their mandates.
“If you want to work in the IEBC, apply. If you wanted to be procurement officers, you should have applied so that you know where ballot papers will be procured from. Those institutions are run by competent Kenyans and we must respect them,” he said.
National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula expressed confidence that Ruto would secure overwhelming support from Bungoma and the wider Western Kenya region in the next General Election.
Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi also voiced confidence in the President’s re-election prospects, declaring: “We want the two terms without a petition.”
Mudavadi credited Ruto with initiating what he described as an infrastructure revolution in the country.
Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka commended the President for what he termed the equitable distribution of development projects across the country, saying the approach would strengthen his political support ahead of the elections.
Later, in Sirisia Constituency, Ruto launched the construction of a modern market and addressed residents in Sirisia town.
He subsequently continued his development tour to Matungu Constituency in Kakamega County and Vihiga.
Those accompanying the President included Cooperatives Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Members of Parliament, Members of County Assemblies and other leaders.

items.summary:
Demolition notices for buildings in Hebron provoke fear among Palestinians
Palestinians fear forced displacement as Israeli authorities target legally licensed homes in a Palestinian-administered area of the occupied West Bank.

items.text:
Demolition notices for buildings in Hebron provoke fear among Palestinians
Palestinians fear forced displacement as Israeli authorities target legally licensed homes in a Palestinian-administered area of the occupied West Bank.
Hebron, Occupied West Bank – Amjad al-Qawasmi stood gazing at the eight-storey residential building he constructed 13 years ago in the heart of Hebron. He struggled to understand how it could be reduced to rubble in a matter of moments.
The building in the southern West Bank is one of two upon which the Israeli army posted demolition notices last Sunday morning, even though both are in Area A, which, under the Oslo Accords, is under full Palestinian control.
The buildings are in the Dairat al-Seer area, in the northwest of Hebron. One contains 25 residential apartments, the other has 40, alongside an adjacent home. The Israeli army has set a one-week deadline for filing objections to the demolition orders.
The Israeli authorities justified the decisions by citing the buildings’ proximity to “Settler Road 35”, despite the structures possessing all the necessary permits from the Palestinian Authority and the Hebron Municipality.
Hebron is divided into a larger area under Palestinian administrative control and a smaller area – housing Israeli settlers – in the centre of the city.
Pervasive fear
The affected families are living in a state of anxiety, fearing that the demolition orders will be carried out. Meanwhile, the property owners have filed formal objections in an attempt to halt the demolitions.
Al-Qawasmi told Al Jazeera that his building was constructed in 2013 at a cost exceeding 18 million shekels ($5.6m). He, along with his father and brother, had prepared the apartments for occupancy from the ground up, installing all necessary utilities after obtaining the required permits from the Ministry of Local Government.
He explained that he, his brothers, and their families live on the lower floors of the building.
Most of the other apartments were sold to families who have yet to complete their payments; a situation exacerbated by the difficult economic conditions they are facing, such as salary cuts and the ban on most Palestinian workers entering Israel for employment, which has been in effect since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.
“Like all the residents of the building, we fear the execution of the demolition order. Although we have hired a lawyer to try to freeze the decision, this is an occupation, anything is possible,” said al-Qawasmi.
The families living in the two buildings have begun packing their essential belongings and clothing into cardboard boxes in anticipation of a potential forced eviction to carry out the demolition. However, they remain uncertain about the fate of their furniture and other possessions, should they not be granted the time to clear out their apartments.
A devastating loss
Samer Abu Hadid purchased a plot of land in the area five years ago and built a villa for his eight-member family. The 1,165 square metre property cost an estimated $3m.
Last Sunday morning, he was shocked when Israeli soldiers stormed the villa and served him a demolition notice, granting him a one-week window to file an objection. The order stated that it was a military decision based on “security grounds”.
“I told the officer that the villa is legally licensed and there are no grounds for its demolition. He simply replied, ‘Look at the document carefully, the reasons are security-related ‘ and added that I have one week to file an objection. But what can I possibly do in one week against an already-issued demolition order?” he asked Al Jazeera.
Abu Hadid reached out to local authorities to follow up on the matter, yet he remains deeply concerned that the demolition order might actually be carried out.
“We literally cannot sleep any more; we think about this constantly. We don’t know whether we should move out our furniture and empty the villa, or stay put. Nothing is clear, and we are at a loss as to what to do,” he said.
Blow to the investment sector
According to a report by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (covering the period from November 2024 to October 2025), Israel targeted 97 Palestinian structures in Area A either through actual demolition or the issuance of demolition orders. This is in addition to 46 structures in Area B, 1,390 in Area C and 240 in occupied East Jerusalem.
The Palestinian Commission Against the Wall and Settlements has documented the issuance of 9,518 demolition or ‘stop-construction’ notices between 2015 and the end of September 2026.
They include 344 notices issued during the first nine months of this year. Hebron governorate tops the list with 2,697 notices issued in the city.
Hebron Municipal Council member Muammar al-Oweiwi told Al Jazeera that the recent demolition notices set a precedent in Hebron by targeting Area A, which should be under the full civil and security control of the Palestinian National Authority. Demolition and stop-construction orders were also issued for a family guesthouse and another building in the Farsh al-Hawa area in Area C.
Al-Oweiwi said that the Hebron Municipality is addressing the matter, in coordination with the property owners’ lawyers, by submitting documentation, including building permits, and pursuing the necessary legal procedures.
He added that the case is now before the Israeli courts; the lawyers requested an immediate stay or freeze on the demolition orders, but Israel has yet to respond.
“The municipality is not merely seeking to freeze the decision, but to have it overturned entirely and to secure official documentation confirming that the demolition of these buildings is unlawful,” he stated.

items.text:
My Monitor Was Cutting My Download Speed by 75%
Somehow I am one of those few very lucky people to have the opportunity of owning a 2.5 gig symmetrical line for my internet. But one day, when I wanted to brag to my equally nerdy friends, shock and horror: 600 Mbps down? Luckily my upload speed was still 2.4 Gbps, so I didn’t lose all my bragging rights, but that’s weird, right? If anything, you’d expect the opposite!
My ISP is pretty cool. It’s run by this one guy (Hey Keith!), and I know I can always message them and they respond promptly, as they did this time. We tried to run through a few debugging steps, they checked on their end, and everything was normal. I tried my work laptop too, same speed.
I didn’t have time for debugging, because I needed to travel 2000 km to the other side of the continent for a family emergency.
But as soon as I got back, I got curious again. What could it be? In retrospect, I now know when it started: when I moved all my connections onto my Studio Display XDR. I wanted to have a one-cable setup, and the monitor offered me that. I’ve had it for half a year now, and I don’t think I’ve ever run a speed test through it. 600 Mbps was more than fast enough for me to never realise I wasn’t getting three quarters of the speed I was paying for 🤦
The setup#
- MacBook Pro M3 Pro
- 2026 Studio Display XDR, with everything plugged into it so switching laptops is one cable
- UGREEN USB-C to 2.5G Ethernet adapter, plugged into the display
- UniFi Dream Router 7, the same one from my WiFi 7 debugging post
What I thought was interesting#
Pings to other wired computers during a download would fail 10% of the time over Ethernet through the adapter plugged into my screen, and 0% of the time over Wi-Fi. What made it stranger was that there were no dropped frame errors in macOS’s logs at all. This was the big hint for me: the adapter was dropping them before the computer could know.
I then plugged the adapter straight into my Mac instead of the monitor, and ran an iperf3 server on my UDR 7: 2.3 Gbps. So the cable, the router and the adapter are all fine? What about fast.com? Perfect speeds there too! 2.2 down and 2.3 up when connected straight in. As soon as I connected it to the display, it was back to 600 down again.
So it’s the display, right? Well, I would find out: sort of yes, sort of no, which is why I wanted to write this blog post. I couldn’t find anything online explaining the exact cause, and it’s quite a cool reason.
The driver and flow control#
The adapter uses a Realtek RTL8156B, which on macOS binds to Apple’s generic USB networking driver. But Realtek ship their own driver on their website, so I thought I’d give that a go! I installed it and, to my surprise, it almost doubled the download speed to 1.1 Gbps, but that was still nowhere close to 2.5. First hint that it couldn’t just be the monitor’s fault.
Then I tried flow control. I had never truly looked into this before, and I think it’s quite neat to know about if you were also ignorant of it like me. Basically, when a device receives Ethernet frames it can’t keep up with, it just drops them. With flow control (it’s something your router or switch has to support), it can send the sender a “pause” frame, and the sender then buffers the data on its side, instead of the receiver (the adapter in this case) on its side. I turned it on in my UniFi console and guess what, download jumped to around 2 Gbps, with upload still at full speed! Yay! Well, not so fast…
I don’t like it always being on, because it can add latency to other systems like my gaming PC. Can you work around it? For sure, you can disable it on those computers, but it’s janky, and it’s another thing I need to remember when my Sauerbraten game starts lagging. I need fewer things to remember, considering I am 30 in a couple of months. My memory is not what it used to be.
But the upload was always fine#
Yeah, isn’t that weird? First of all, it looks like the port can indeed do 2.5 in both directions. I already knew that, because I get much more than that from my external SSD through the monitor’s Thunderbolt port. So the issue is not the monitor again? But it has to be!
Well, I had another idea. How about I connect to my Linux box, which is also on 2.5, and send perfectly smooth UDP traffic at a fixed rate with flow control off? Then I can check the chip’s own counter of dropped frames:
So basically no drops whatsoever when connected straight to my Mac, but loads of drops after about 168k frames per second (roughly 2 Gbps). Remember that number. That number comes from the adapter’s own counters: however much I sent, the number of frames it managed to hand over to the Mac each second flattened out at about 168,000, and everything above that was dropped.
Why did this not happen on my SSD? What was the only difference I could find? Bursts!
When the Mac reads data from a USB 3 device, the device sends some packets, then has to wait for the Mac to say “lgtm, send more!”. The SSD enclosure sends 16 packets before needing a go-ahead message back. The RTL8156B in my Ethernet adapter sends 4.
Here is a diagram of my best understanding of why this is an issue. I made this diagram 100 times, and I think I can probably improve it more, but if it helps you understand the issue, I have done my job.
As you can see, the speed of packets coming into the adapter is 2.5 Gbps. That’s what the router pushes in. The speed going out is around 2 Gbps. The reason is that if you add up the average time it takes to get the go-ahead through my monitor’s hub, which is around 7.6 µs, to the average time it takes to send 4 KB, around 8.2 µs, you can find what the maximum speed is.
Well, if the speed of the drain from my adapter to my Mac is half a gig slower than the speed of the input, then you can imagine the buffer getting filled more and more until it overflows. Those are dropped packets, which result in a hard backoff when the router resends them, so you drop loads in speed. And

items.title: Gachagua admits joining Ruto’s UDA was a costly mistake
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21- DCP party leader Rigathi Gachagua has admitted that joining President William Ruto’s UDA party instead of maintaining an independent political vehicle was one of the biggest mistakes he made while in government.
Gachagua said the decision weakened his political position and le
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 21- DCP party leader Rigathi Gachagua has admitted that joining President William Ruto’s UDA party instead of maintaining an independent political vehicle was one of the biggest mistakes he made while in government.
Gachagua said the decision weakened his political position and left him unable to protect his interests when his relationship with Ruto deteriorated, eventually leading to his removal from office.
Speaking while hosting a delegation from Gatundu North at his Wamunyoro residence, the former Deputy President recalled how he entered into a political agreement with Ruto when the President already had his own party, arguing that he should have maintained a separate political outfit.
“We ran into trouble by going to a wedding in someone else’s vehicle. When we got to the venue, he told us to get down, and we ran into problems,” Gachagua said.
He used the analogy to explain why he believes politicians should have their own parties rather than depend on political vehicles controlled by others.
According to Gachagua, having an independent party with more than 100 MPs would have given him greater bargaining power and made it difficult for Ruto to sideline him.
“If we had a party, with more than 100 members of parliament, this Kasongo would be respecting us,” he said.
Gachagua further claimed that he could still be serving as Deputy President had he maintained his own political party instead of joining UDA.
“Even if I made an agreement with him while he had UDA, if we had our own party, up to today I would still be in office,” he added.
The DCP leader said his new party would give him the political independence he lacked during his time in government, allowing him to negotiate from a position of strength and protect the interests of his supporters.
“Now we have our own vehicle, and that’s how we’ll get there, get into government, and protect our affairs inside,” he declared.
He also outlined his party’s priorities, promising to push for legislation that protects farmers, traders and other economic groups.
Gachagua said the party would focus on better laws covering tea, coffee, milk, avocados, macadamia, businesses and livestock feeds.
He called on supporters to elect more DCP candidates to Parliament, arguing that a strong parliamentary presence would give the party greater influence in government.
“We must have good representatives in Parliament from our party, with a large number of us,” he said.

The office was reportedly defaced overnight, with graffiti bearing the words
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 21 – An office belonging to the Linda Mwananchi Movement in Matungu, Kakamega County, has been vandalised ahead of President William Ruto’s visit to the constituency scheduled for Saturday, November 21.
The office was reportedly defaced overnight, with graffiti bearing the words “TWO TERMS” and “TUTAM” written on the premises, in an incident that has drawn condemnation from Bumula MP Wanami Wamboka.
Wamboka, who serves as the Linda Mwananchi Movement’s Secretary for Public Policy, described the incident as political intimidation and said it would not deter the movement from conducting its activities in the area.
In a statement, the legislator said the vandalism happened ahead of the President’s scheduled tour, accusing those responsible of attempting to intimidate supporters of the movement.
“Our Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) office in Matungu was overnight defaced ahead of Mr President’s scheduled tour of the area,” Wamboka said.
He termed the incident an act of political intolerance, insisting that the movement would not be intimidated or silenced by the destruction of its property.
“This cowardly act of political intolerance and intimidation will not shake our resolve or silence the people’s voice,” he added.
Wamboka further announced that leaders associated with Linda Mwananchi would travel to Matungu as a team to stand with their supporters despite the incident.
“We shall visit Matungu as a team, stand with our supporters and reaffirm our commitment to the people-driven movement,” he said.
The vandalism comes as Ruto continues an eight-day tour of Western Kenya, which has included engagements in Busia, Bungoma and Kakamega counties.
According to the published presidential itinerary, the Head of State is scheduled to visit Matungu on Saturday, November 21, where he is expected to lay the foundation stone for Kenya Medical Training College hostels and launch the Matungu-River Sio Road project.
The President’s visit is part of his wider development and political engagements in the Western region.
Wamboka maintained that the incident would not weaken the movement’s presence in the area, declaring that attacks on its offices would not erase the political aspirations of its supporters.
“You can deface our offices, but you cannot deface the people’s resolve for change. Linda Mwananchi! Linda Kenya!” he said.

items.title: Australia complete record T20I chase at MCG to edge England in thriller
items.summary:
Australia beat England in first T20I as MCG record run-chase earns hosts 1-0 lead in five-match series
Harry Brook hits 68 off 25 balls after being dropped twice, as Australia put down six chances in the field; England add only 68 from final 10 overs, as hosts chase 188 with a ball to spare; second
items.text:
Australia beat England in first T20I as MCG record run-chase earns hosts 1-0 lead in five-match series
Harry Brook hits 68 off 25 balls after being dropped twice, as Australia put down six chances in the field; England add only 68 from final 10 overs, as hosts chase 188 with a ball to spare; second T20I takes place in Carrara on Tuesday (play starts 8.15am UK time)
Saturday 21 November 2026 12:06, UK
Australia pulled off a record T20I run chase of 188 at the MCG to beat England by three wickets with a ball to spare in a thrilling series opener in Melbourne on Saturday.
England captain Harry Brook had tonked 68 off just 25 balls - hitting six sixes - as England posted 187-9, though his side wasted a dominant position of 119-4 at the halfway point of their innings by adding only 68 from the last 10 overs.
Nikhil Chaudhary, who had helped drag Australia back into the contest with the ball - the hosts having dropped six chances - then top-scored with a magnificent 68 off 38 with the bat.
He was dismissed with 20 still required off the final two overs, Australia seven down, but Jack Edwards (25no off 11) struck a couple of crucial sixes in a clutch cameo before finishing the job with a boundary.
After being inserted by the hosts, England's innings had got off to the worst possible start as Phil Salt picked out mid-off first ball, while Aneurin Donald (10) - put down two deliveries prior - perished soon after.
But Brook, dropped on 2 and 3, made Australia pay for their profligacy as he smoked three sixes in a row in taking Riley Meredith's fourth over for 24, the touring captain romping to a 20-ball fifty.
He and Tom Banton (39 off 22) - shelled twice, taking Australia's tally to five inside seven overs - put on 107 for the third wicket, with Adam Zampa also taking some tap as his opening over went for 20.
Both were gone in the space of six deliveries though, Chaudhary's wrist spin accounting for Brook, caught behind, and Banton gone to a sensational diving catch in the deep by debutant Lachlan Shaw.
England stumbled their way to a rather underwhelming score thereafter, despite the best efforts of Jordan Cox (27 off 20) and Sam Curran (21 off 20), the visitors falling short of the 200-run target they'll have surely been eyeing.
That said, it was still a record T20I chase at the MCG for Australia to reel in, and their assignment was made all the tougher when Liam Dawson (1-30) struck in the opening over - Jake Fraser-McGurk (1) bowled when charging the left-arm spinner, deceived in the flight.
Mitch Marsh hammered Henry Crocombe's first ball in T20 international cricket for six over deep backward square for quite the introduction, but the young quick responded well to remove fellow debutant Sam Harper (32 off 15) for his first wicket in his second over.
Harper had provided some impetus to the Australian innings, Jamie Overton's opening over plundered for 21 runs, and Chaudhary maintained that momentum, with useful support from his captain Marsh (37 off 32) and Tim David (20 off 13).
David failed to cash in a huge slice of luck when the bails failed to dislodge as he inside-edged one back onto his stumps, as he departed a ball later to the returning Adil Rashid (1-30).
It prompted a rather sizeable Australian wobble, with three wickets tumbling for 13 runs in little more than an over, and when Chaudhary finally fell - caught in the deep - it looked like England might be in the ascendency, only for Edwards to have other ideas.
In other worrying news for England, Will Jacks left the field late on, splitting the webbing on his hand as Ben Dwarshuis drilled a ball back at him in the penultimate over. He is due to captain the team in the fifth and final T20I of the series as Brook departs for the Test tour of South Africa.
Chaudhary enjoyed 'chirp' with England
Player of the Match, Nikhil Chaudhary:
"I was just trying to hit the wickets at the start and got the big wicket of Harry [Brook]. I wanted to bowl that five, six-metre length. That was my goal.
"With the bat, you knew it was going to be a big game and that there was going to some chirp. I just had to stay stable and play my game.
"Hopefully I did that and won the game for the team, which was great. There is nothing better than playing at the MCG and winning."
Brook: England were 10 runs short
England captain Harry Brook:
"It was a very entertaining game, going down to the last couple of balls. It's what the fans want to see and everybody watching at home.
"We were probably 10 runs short of what we needed on that surface. If we get those, we probably end up winning the game."
'I was worried when we dropped Brook twice!'
Australia captain Mitch Marsh:
"I was worried when we dropped the best batter in the world [Brook] a couple of times. Most of the time you don't deserve to win.
"But outside a few tough chances, I thought the energy and speed was great to watch. They are all good kids.
"It has been a pretty crazy 12 days but right there is the future of the Australian cricket side with all these young guys. Hopefully we can get back to enjoying that.
"They are a great bunch. I want them to not care about making mistakes and enjoy the environment. Hopefully a win like that shows them they belong."
Results/schedule for England's Australia tour
All T20 internationals to start at 8.15am UK time
- First ODI: Australia won by seven wickets in Perth
- Second ODI: England won by 135 runs in Adelaide
- Third ODI: England won by 97 runs in Hobart
- First T20I: Australia won by three wickets in Melbourne
- Second T20I: Tuesday November 24 (Carrara)
- Third T20I: Friday November 27 (Brisbane)
- Fourth T20I: Sunday November 29 (Sydney)
- Fifth T20I: Wednesday December 2 (Canberra)

items.summary:
A rundown of the big Pochettino to Man United news
Mauricio Pochettino told the Manchester United hierarchy he wants a say in all major decisions related to the first team. The club’s transfer business in recent years has received plenty of criticism and the new head coach is eager for a level of co
items.text:
A rundown of the big Pochettino to Man United news
Mauricio Pochettino told the Manchester United hierarchy he wants a say in all major decisions related to the first team. The club’s transfer business in recent years has received plenty of criticism and the new head coach is eager for a level of control not enjoyed by his recent predecessors.
Pochettino has been given the title of head coach rather than manager but has made plain the power he is seeking, working alongside the director of football, Jason Wilcox, who is in overall charge of player recruitment.
“The way that we work is indifferent to the title description,” Pochettino said. “It depends on the structure, depends on the communication, the relationship with all the areas. I know that being a head coach I am the guy that is going to decide tomorrow the squad for Sunday and I’m going to pick the starting XI. I’m going to make the changes, and of course in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad. In the end, Manchester United is a football club.”
A drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session on Thursday has apologised for what he called a “total error of judgment” and removed the footage from his YouTube channel.
He said: “I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”
Our man David Hytner has assessed Pochettino’s management style, arguing the Argentinian excelled in man-management – but says he will need his powers to energise new squad and impress owners.
He wrote: “Pochettino will love how the United support stand behind their manager, especially in troublesome times. He will love the pageantry and event glamour of Old Trafford. And he will love having Ferguson in the crowd for the matches.”
Before I get onto Pochettino and United, I’ve just seen a highlights edit on Twitter X of Premier League wingers between 2015 and 2020: Rihad Mahrez, Leroy Sane, Mo Salah, Sadio Mane, Alexis Sanchez, Raheem Sterling … was that a truly golden age of wide men in the English top flight? Many of them were inverted, of course, but they were box office.
It certainly feels like wingers are slightly less important now. Antoine Semenyo and Bukayo Saka are probably the leading men, but that sprinkle of star dust in wide positions has faded somewhat. Am I talking nonsense, or is there something in that argument? Pop me or the matchday live address an email.
Find more Premier League news in The Talk. This week it includes bits from David Moyes on Jack Grealish and Andoni Iraola on Liverpool’s clash with Manchester United, as well as more from Alonso and Maresca.
Enzo Maresca has said he may need to tweak the balance of Manchester City’s midfield.
City have suffered three consecutive defeats in the league, having begun the campaign with seven wins on the bounce, and are third in the table, six points off leaders Arsenal, and face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium at lunchtime today.
“For sure there are things we need to do better in terms of balance,” Maresca said. “But the same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same midfield that lost three games in a row.
“We won games with Enzo, we lost games with Enzo. I know that when there is a defeat, we are all looking for the reason why. Sometimes we probably need more balance, we need different kinds of players. [It] depends a little bit on the game. The idea is to continue in attack in the same way, creating chances, but finding a balance when we defend.”
Xabi Alonso has admitted Chelsea’s injury list is a concern. The club have a lighter schedule after their failure to qualify for Europe but are struggling to keep players fit and have a host of selection issues before today’s home game against Leeds.
João Pedro is yet to return from a thigh injury, Reece James is unlikely to recover from knee surgery until the new year and Maxence Lacroix is out with a long-term hamstring injury. Jorrel Hato and Jamie Gittens are also unavailable.
“It’s a concern,” Alonso said of the injuries. “Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.
“I [have to] adapt to the circumstances. With the injuries you don’t have a choice. Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu.”
Mauricio Pochettino was obviously the big draw on yesterday’s Premier League press conference callsheet, but there was some other news via some other more familiar faces in terms of this season’s managerial lineup.
I’ll run through some of those news lines before pivoting to big Poch’s big United unveiling.
Dominic here. Morning all. Let’s get straight into it, shall we?
Bayern Munich and England were rocked by the news last night, confirmed by the Bundesliga champions, that will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted after 20 minutes and his Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, said the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.
Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired Cologne ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half in a further blow to Kompany’s men.
Dominic will be here shortly ahead of a busy Saturday of Premier League and Women’s Super League action.
The Premier League returns after the men’s international break with Manchester City hoping to get back on track after three consecutive defeats in the league when they host Fulham in today’s 12.30 kick-off (all times GMT). The afternoon kick-offs include Chelsea v Leeds, Spurs v Ipswich and Thomas Frank’s first match in charge as Crystal Palace take on Coventry. Then at 5.30pm, Arsenal head to Tyneside to take on Newcastle.

items.summary:
The Chelsea loanee turning heads and Championship defenders at 17
- Published
Explosive pace, infectious energy on the field and bundles of footballing ability.
At just 17, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen has looked at home in the Championship since embarking on his first loan move away from Chelsea.
With one s
items.text:
The Chelsea loanee turning heads and Championship defenders at 17
- Published
Explosive pace, infectious energy on the field and bundles of footballing ability.
At just 17, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen has looked at home in the Championship since embarking on his first loan move away from Chelsea.
With one senior appearance to his name at Stamford Bridge, the winger swapped west London for the south coast in August and has quickly become a fan favourite at Fratton Park.
Indeed, Kavuma-McQueen was so impressive in a recent game against Sheffield United, Pompey boss John Mousinho admitted their tactic essentially became - pass him the ball as much as possible.
"For a 17-year-old to come in and play as many games as he has done is a real achievement," the Portsmouth head coach told BBC Sport.
"He's been brilliant to work with and has been absolutely unplayable in some games, for us it's now about getting him consistently to that level.
"It's very easy to forget that he's only 17 because of the way that he plays and how he carries himself - overall it's been an excellent loan so far and we're really excited to see how he goes for the rest of the season."
At international level, Kavuma-McQueen has played 31 matches for England's youth sides and scored 29 goals.
One of his most recent for England Under-18s was a stunning strike that saw him beat a number of defenders with some smart footwork before launching a right-footed rocket into the top corner from 25 yards.
For Portsmouth, he scored seven minutes into his first Championship start and has registered two assists, contributing to winning points for the Blues in games against Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United.
"No other so-called 'big six' Premier League club has a fully homegrown 17-year-old on loan in the Championship," said BBC football news reporter Nizaar Kinsella.
"This is a source of pride within Chelsea's academy. At Championship level, only Preston's George Gryba and Wolves' Charlie Holt have made appearances at a younger age this season.
"It is clear that Kavuma-McQueen finds playing against opponents of his own age relatively straightforward.
"Securing a loan move was so important this summer, without European football, and with a large number of wide options available, opportunities were always likely to be limited at Chelsea."
So far this season, Kavuma-McQueen has featured predominantly on the left but has also played on the right wing of Portsmouth's attack.
He leads the Championship in some attacking metrics, completing the most successful take-ons (30) and attempting the joint-most dribbles (55) in the division.
He is also in the top 10 for drives into the box and carries ending in shots.
The Blues have a number of wide attackers to choose from, with Abu Kamara and Josh Murphy both proven at this level, but the teenager has displayed his credentials to play in their starting XI, making nine starts in the Championship with a further five appearances off the bench.
If he can remain fit then he will undoubtably be an important player for the rest of the 2026-27 campaign, but a sustained period of health is far from straightforward in a relentless league and a busy festive schedule to come.
Regardless of the impact that Kavuma-McQueen has over the rest of the season, there is no doubt that the experience he will gain from this loan should serve him well going forward.
Character shown in injury
Mousinho has praised the winger's character after an injury setback in September after falling over advertising hoardings at Fratton Park.
He suffered a double fracture on his right hand, but opted against surgery and now wears a splint and cast for games which has delayed his full recovery to around eight weeks.
The Portsmouth boss admitted that he was probably not managing the injury in the most ideal way, but believed his decision to play on provided an insight into his mentality of wanting to make the most of the loan move.
"From a football perspective he's managing it unbelievably well and he hasn't shied away from anything on the pitch," Mousinho added.
"It's never been a concern of mine and the fact that he wanted to play and didn't want surgery tells us everything we need to know about the lad."
Pompey are enjoying a positive start to their third season back in the second tier having won promotion from League One in 2024.
They are 11th in the table and just two points outside of the newly expanded play-off positions.
Kavuma-McQueen has played plenty of minutes already - his 719 is comfortably the highest among Championship players 18 and under, but there is a slight concern Pompey could become victims of his success in terms of his immediate future.
"Arguably in the first part of Portsmouth's season, he was their best player," said BBC Radio Solent commentator Andrew Moon.
"He's fast, skillful and exciting to watch. He's also able to cope with a physical league that most teenagers can't.
"His output did drop off before the international break but there will always be some ups and downs with such a young player. Mousinho has been managing his minutes very carefully.
"He's already being watched by other clubs and Chelsea could recall him in January to send elsewhere. Portsmouth will argue strongly that Fratton Park is the best place for him to continue his development."
Chelsea in touch 'all the time'
For his parent club, Kavuma-McQueen is seen as a talent with a genuine chance of making it at the club, despite fierce competition among the wide players already in the squad.
He joined the west London club at under-eight level and signed a scholarship in July 2025.
Prior to his move to the south coast he travelled with the senior Chelsea squad for their pre-season tour, starting against Western Sydney Wanderers down-under before his loan move.
Chelsea already have a host of highly-rated teenagers out on loan, including Jesse Derry (Sporting), Dastan Satpayev (Burnley), Reggie Walsh (Wigan Athletic), Shim Mheuka (Celtic) and Landon Emenalo

items.text:
Las Vegas GP: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff insists George Russell had 'perfect' track position in qualifying amid questions over tow
Kimi Antonelli was fastest in Las Vegas GP Qualifying but will start from sixth because of a grid penalty; George Russell will start from second after finishing third; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Saturday 21 November 2026 08:58, UK
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff dismissed suggestions the team should have done more to aid George Russell's bid for Las Vegas Grand Prix pole as he insisted the British driver had "perfect" track position for his final run in qualifying.
Russell had gone into the final part of qualifying as the favourite for pole but ultimately finished third after his team-mate Kimi Antonelli topped Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
Many had assumed Mercedes would use Antonelli, who has already sealed the Drivers' Championship and is serving a five-place grid penalty in Las Vegas, to give Russell a tow up the main straight to help him in his bid to chase down Verstappen for second in the drivers' standings.
- Las Vegas GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
- F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column
- Got the Sky Sports app? Sign up for latest F1 alerts📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺
Instead, a frantic finish to qualifying saw the Mercedes duo and several other cars in a scrap for track position, which left Antonelli at the back of the pack scrambling to start his lap before the session ended, but then benefitting from a huge multi-car tow to go fastest.
Speaking to Sky Sports F1 pundit and former Aston Martin head of strategy Bernie Collins after the session, Wolff admitted he was shocked Antonelli had taken pole given the Italian had to closely follow Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad around the lap.
"We have absolutely no clue," Wolff said. "And you (Collins) as a strategist, you know we thought Kimi was either going to miss the lap or he's going to be way too close to Lindblad.
"He crossed the line 1.4 seconds behind, and that was basically it. So, I don't understand how being that close you can even do this time.
"If you're 1.4 seconds behind the car in front, you would think this is too close, especially with a car that went eight tenths slower, but for whatever reason, that works."
Asked why Mercedes hadn't prioritised giving Russell a tow, Wolff suggested that a driver error, rather than the team's strategy, had cost the Brit pole.
"Actually, George, for me, had the perfect position," Wolff said. "He was four seconds behind the car in front.
"We need to find out because I think there was some kind of… turn seven-eight-nine, whether that was a mistake or something else happened.
"We need to… I don't know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap, because he was quickest all the time."
Villeneuve: Mercedes didn't do anything to help Russell
Former world champion Jacques Villeneuve suggested that Antonelli "went out of his way" to avoid giving Russell a tow.
"The team didn't do anything to help Russell," the Sky Sports F1 pundit said.
"When Toto says Russell was four seconds behind and he was in a good position, that was from his (Russell's) doing. The team did not help him.
"He kind of skated the answer there. Because Kimi went out of his way to make sure he wasn't ahead of Russell, to make sure he wouldn't help his team-mate, and that was obvious.
"He played his own card, he played his own game even though he knew that he couldn't get pole in the end.
"That was a little bit nasty, and George will be really, really upset. Mostly when, Antonelli has got the world championship, the team has got the championship, they had every interest in helping George."
Sky Sports F1's Jamie Chadwick was also surprised that Russell wasn't given more support.
"I think the reality is that, regardless of where those two Mercedes found themselves, for me it just felt like the order should have been Kimi in front of George," Chadwick said.
"If they were at the front of the pack like Red Bull were, that's one thing, and then George would have benefitted from Kimi. If they were at the back of the pack, then he could have benefitted like Kimi did at the end."
Russell: We'll take it offline
Following the first Q3 runs, after which Russell was third behind Verstappen and McLaren's Lando Norris, he had asked over team radio whether the team could get Antonelli to help him.
Despite that not materialising, Russell was not critical of his team or team-mate when asked about the situation after the session.
He told Sky Sports F1: "It's so difficult to orchestrate and getting the perfect tow is high risk.
"Kimi, if he started his lap a second later wouldn't have got the lap in and, in the end, he gained a second in the straight - maybe more - and maybe lost six tenths in the corners. So, it's unbelievable the impact.
Asked during the post-session press conference for the top three whether he was hoping for more assistance from Antonelli, Russell added: "No, I mean, obviously, it's still important, if you've got a grid penalty, to start as high up the order as possible.
"But we'll take it offline and we can talk about it."
Antonelli: I thought I was screwed
Antonelli, who will start the race from sixth on the grid, suggested he was unhappy that Mercedes had left himself and Russell leading other cars in Q3.
"Well, first thing, as George said, we will talk about it because we've been sent out at the front in qualifying always," Antonelli said.
The 20-year-old explained the range of emotions he went through as he dropped to the back of the pack, barely made the line in time, and then contended with closely following Lindblad through the corners.
He added: "About Turn 5, it was fully on me. Like I said, we were three-wide, first of all, and I just said, 'you know what? I'm just going to back off.'

12.55 Ascot - Doyen Quest and Blow Your Wad clash
Doyen Quest and Blow Your Wad headline a classy field for the Ladbrokes 1965 Chase at Ascot.
Dan Skelton's Doyen Quest outpointed Blow Your Wad when claiming the Grade Two Oaksey Chase at Sandown on his final start last season but could only manage third of three on his return at Carlisle. With that run behind him he ought to be sharper here.
Blow Your Wad should handle this quicker ground and, having progressed through the grades last season, warrants respect as he receives weight under Freddie Mitchell.

Master Chewy completes the quartet.
1.30 Ascot - Classy hurdlers Lucky Place and Kateira head field
Classy hurdlers Lucky Place and Kateira clash in a trappy edition of the Grade Two Ladbrokes Ascot Hurdle.
Lucky Place took this race in 2024 and, having tried fencing, he reverted to hurdles with a few solid runs including when runner-up in the Grade Two Select Hurdle at Sandown. Third behind Alexei in the Molyneux at Aintree on his reappearance, this extra distance should be more to his liking.

items.title: 'Somebody’s got to stand up to that guy' - Russell slams Verstappen after clash
items.summary:
George Russell hits out at Max Verstappen after Las Vegas GP clash and says 'somebody's got to stand up to that guy'
Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' George Russell to start on front of Las Vegas grid, as Toto Wolff predicts "big cinema"; Russell hit out at rival after final practice collisio
items.text:
George Russell hits out at Max Verstappen after Las Vegas GP clash and says 'somebody's got to stand up to that guy'
Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' George Russell to start on front of Las Vegas grid, as Toto Wolff predicts "big cinema"; Russell hit out at rival after final practice collision; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Saturday 21 November 2026 07:30, UK
George Russell launched a scathing criticism of Max Verstappen after a collision between them in final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix ahead of a race they will now start on the front row together.
The pair, who have had run-ins in the past on track in recent years, clashed wheels in final practice as they fought over track position.
Verstappen first overtook Russell on the run down The Strip to Turn 14 before the Mercedes went back down the inside of the Red Bull in the braking zone, with the two cars brushing wheels.

Stewards investigated the incident and issued a warning to Verstappen, ruling he had been "driving erratically" under braking into the corner once ahead of the Mercedes, which had been preparing for a timed lap.
Verstappen and Russell went on to qualify second and third respectively, which becomes first and second on the grid for Sunday's race at 4am, live on Sky Sports F1, due to Q3 pacesetter Kimi Antonelli's five-place grid penalty.
Asked after qualifying about the decision made by stewards, Russell said "a warning was fine" before going on to issue a withering rebuke of his Red Bull rival's approach.
Russell told Sky Italy: "There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it.
"I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."
Russell's comments about wanting to "stand up to" Verstappen echoed those he made following an incident between them in qualifying at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix.
The pair traded barbs in person and via interviews after that clash, when Verstappen was given a one-place grid drop for impeding Russell in Q3, with the Mercedes driver then launching an explosive attack on his rival ahead of the following week's race in Abu Dhabi.
After qualifying in Las Vegas, the pair appeared together in the post-race press conference and were asked about the impact and whether there had any confusion about the 'gentleman's agreement' between drivers regarding not disturbing a rival who was about to start a flying lap.
Verstappen said "nothing happened", while Russell said there was "no confusion, I think it was pretty clear".
What did the pundits make of the clash and Russell's comments?
Sky Sports F1's Jacques Villeneuve said of the incident itself: "Fun and exciting to watch! But we want to see this in the race, not in free practice. Unnecessary.
"Once you've lost your track position, too bad for you. If you're George, you got overtaken, it's practice. OK, you don't get it back, you lost your position and move on.
"That was a completely unnecessary risk. You don't want to make an enemy of Max."
Speaking after hearing Russell's post-qualifying comments, Sky Sports F1's Jamie Chadwick said: "George saying he'll stand up to Max, I like that. It's very reminiscent of what we saw in Qatar.
"With George we know he's never going to give to Max. I think Max does try his luck with that kind of thing and that is why he is able to find himself in good positions. It comes also from the pit wall, who are telling him to push through the traffic and fight his way to get clear air, and he's aggressive and he does bully people out of the way.
"Most people do give in to that and then someone like Liam Lawson [at the Mexico City GP] comes along, doesn't, and gets in trouble from the big team.
"I quite like the fact that George is standing up to him because Max does it intentionally, he drives like that. There is something good to be said for that, but there's also something that needs to be fought against."
With the pair now starting together on the front row for the short run to Las Vegas' first corner, Villeneuve added: "No love lost there, so that's good before the start for tomorrow! That will make it exciting.
"He shouldn't overtake someone who is about to start his lap, true, but how does that person know you're about to start your lap? That's one thing, and maybe you're about to start your own lap yourself.
"So that's a difficult one to judge, ultimately."
Wolff predicts 'big cinema' for Verstappen vs Russell race start
Sunday will be the first time that Verstappen and Russell have shared the front row of a Grand Prix grid this year.
Both drivers are in the five-way fight for second place in the Drivers' Championship, with Verstappen currently holding the position by 17 points from third-placed Russell.
Asked what he was expecting at the start of the race, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports F1: "Big cinema!
"If they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching."
Verstappen is chasing a third win in six races, and a third in four years on Las Vegas' Strip Circuit, and is ready for a challenge.
"Feeling good but, at the same time, also aware that Mercedes is quick," he told Sky Sports F1. "So we need to really try and fight.
"I think it's not going to be very easy, but I don't mind it to be tough. We'll see. I hope that just it is an exciting race."
